title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

title: Directed triangles in oriented graphs without a directed cycle of length $3t$
abstract: For integers $k,\ell\ge 3$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_k,\Cdir_\ell)$ denote the maximum number of directed cycles of length $k$ in an $n$-vertex oriented graph containing no directed cycles of length $\ell$. Grzesik, Jaworska, Kielak, Kuc and Ślusarczyk~\cite{GJ} systematically studied the generalized Turán problem for directed cycles and conjectured that, for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_3,\Cdir_{3t})=\frac{t-1}{4}n^2+o(n^2)$. They proved this asymptotic formula for $t=2$. In this paper, we prove it for every fixed integer $t\ge 3$, thereby confirming the conjecture.

title: Finite volume neural networks for singularly perturbed boundary value problems
abstract: We develop a singular-layer enhanced Finite Volume Neural Network (sl-FVNN) methodology for solving singularly perturbed boundary value problems. The proposed framework combines flux-conserving finite volume residuals with analytically derived boundary layer correctors, enabling stable and efficient approximation of sharp boundary variations induced by small perturbation parameters. Numerical experiments over a broad range of small perturbation parameters ($10^{-4}$ to $10^{-12}$), demonstrate that the sl-FVNN yields uniformly accurate predicted solutions and significantly improved convergence behavior compared to conventional FVNN methods. Further comparisons with sl-PINNs from (Gie, Hong, Jung, Appl. Anal. 2024) show that our sl-FVNNs attain comparable accuracy for reaction--diffusion and Burgers equations, while achieving significantly improved convergence for convection-dominated nonlinear problems. These results highlight the effectiveness of incorporating asymptotic layer structures into finite volume based neural networks, offering a practical and scalable framework for multiscale PDE learning in stiff regimes.

title: A nonlinear multigrid method for the preconditioned lattice Boltzmann equation
abstract: This work developed a preconditioned lattice Boltzmann equation (PLBE) smoother for the residual-driven full approximation scheme (FAS) multigrid to accelerate steady-state LBE calculations. To overcome the deterioration of LBE smoothing at low viscosity, we used a two- relaxation-time (TRT) collision model together with characteristic-velocity and kinetic precondition- ing to keep the relaxation frequency for the even-order moments within a favorable range, while independently selecting the relaxation frequency for the odd-order moments to reduce their local amplification factor. We further investigated F-, W-, and hybrid V/W-cycles to address residual stagnation observed with V-cycles at high Reynolds numbers. The 2D lid-driven cavity flow was used as a test case. At Re = 5000, TRT-PLBE-FAS achieves an approximately 27-fold speedup over single-grid TRT-PLBE. At Re = 20000 on a 20482 grid, the hybrid V/W-cycle reduces solution time by 14% compared with the W-cycle.

title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
abstract:
A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces.
  Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored.
  Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others.
  The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.

title: Finite-Time Blow-up for the Radial Mass-Critical Fractional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
abstract: We prove that radial negative-energy strong solutions to the focusing mass-critical fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu=(-Δ)^su-|u|^{4s/N}u, \quad N\ge2,\quad \frac12<s<1, \] blow up in finite time. This resolves the finite-time blow-up versus infinite-time grow-up alternative left open by Boulenger, Himmelsbach and Lenzmann in the mass-critical regime. The argument uses an exponentially localized virial field together with a dyadic resolvent estimate that transfers the resulting weighted Balakrishnan energy to localized fractional Sobolev norms. When $s\ge N/(2N-1)$, we extend the conclusion to radial $H^s$ solutions by establishing the integrated virial identity at energy regularity. As a consequence, mass-critical ground-state standing waves are strongly unstable by finite-time blow-up.

title: Supersaturation and reconfiguration diameter of independent transversals
abstract: Consider the collection of independent transversals of a vertex-partitioned graph of maximum degree $Δ$. It is a classic result that when all parts have size at least $2Δ$, the collection is nonempty. Recently, it was found that if the parts have size at least $2Δ+1$, then every pair of independent transversals is connected, within the collection, by a sequence of one-vertex reconfigurations. We prove, among other results, that there are exponentially many independent transversals when the parts have size at least $2Δ$, and that the reconfiguration diameter is at most linear in the number of parts when the parts have size at least $4Δ$.

title: Projector-Based Conic Formulations and Exact Decompositions for Continuous Multifacility Location
abstract: We study the continuous multisource facility location problem, where facility locations and the assignment of demand points must be determined simultaneously. We show that the assignment structure can be represented by orthogonal projection matrices. This observation leads to new mixed-projection conic formulations that avoid the big-M envelopes used in standard mixed-integer models. Based on these formulations, we develop exact decomposition algorithms that separate the discrete selection of the assignment projectors from location convex conic subproblems. We also derive semidefinite relaxation bounds and primal procedures that provide warm starts for the exact methods. The proposed approach draws new connections between continuous multifacility location, orthogonal projectors, and low-rank semidefinite optimization, and applies to general conic-representable distances.

title: Gorenstein linkage of ideals and doubly layered filtrations of MCM modules
abstract: The glicci conjecture asks whether every Cohen-Macaulay ideal in a regular ring belongs to the Gorenstein linkage class of a complete intersection. We show that the corresponding statement is false for nonregular rings. We prove that the conjecture holds for zero-dimensional ideals and for ideals of dimensions one and two in polynomial rings. Geometrically, this implies that every zero-dimensional subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n_k$, as well as every curve in $\mathbb{P}^n_k$, is glicci. We also prove that every Cohen-Macaulay monomial ideal is glicci. Our approach involves reducing the problem to height-two ideals and studying their N-type resolutions and the filtrations of the associated modules. We also show that every orientable maximal Cohen-Macaulay module over a two-dimensional Gorenstein ring is stably isomorphic to a doubly layered module. Finally, we prove that every ideal belongs to the Gorenstein linkage class of a Golod ideal.

title: Finite time blow-up for the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori
abstract: We show that the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori of revolution produces a finite time singularity, provided the initial energy is below $12π$. Our approach relies on the connection with elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane and a fine analysis of Palais--Smale sequences in the relevant energy regime.

title: Finitely generated groups with arbitrarily fast MIF growth
abstract: A group $G$ is mixed identity free, or MIF, if for each nontrivial $w(x)\in G\star (\mathbb{Z}=\langle x\rangle)$ there is some $g\in G$ such that $w(g)\neq 1$. Associated to MIF groups is a natural growth function that measures how far in the Cayley graph one witnesses such inequations. We adapt a recent construction of the author with Hyde to show that for each function $f:\mathbf{N}\to \mathbf{N}$ there is a finitely generated group $G$ whose MIF growth function grows faster than $f$. This answers a question first considered by Henry Bradford. As a consequence, we also provide the first examples of finitely generated MIF groups that are not selfless, answering a question of Bradford and Sisto.

title: Quantitative unique continuation for semiclassical Witten-Schrödinger type operator with low regular coefficients
abstract: In this note we study eigenfunctions localization of the semiclassical selfadjoint Schrödinger operator with low regular coefficients on domains of $\mathbb{R}^2$. We show a unique continuation result on the local decay of the eigenfunction: local supremum on open sets can't vanish faster than global supremum on these same sets times an exponential term that decrease in the semiclassical limit $h\to 0$ as $\exp(-c\log(1/h)/h)$ in the worst case. We deduce from this result a control on the eigenfunctions of the semiclassical Schrödinger operator on a $W^{2,\infty}$ compact Riemann surface with Lipschitz positive metric and with Robin boundary condition. This last part leads us to study the Schrödinger operator with a Witten Laplacian.

title: A general theorem on the analytic spread and associated primes of divisorial filtrations
abstract: We prove that a classical theorem of McAdam about the analytic spread of an ideal in a Noetherian local ring $R$ is true for rational divisorial filtrations on an arbitrary Noetherian local ring. We deduce McAdam's original theorem from our result. This generalizes earlier work by the author, showing that this theorem is true for rational divisorial filtrations, with the restriction that $R$ is an equidimensional local ring which is essentially of finite type over an excellent local ring of dimension $\le 3$.

title: Translation surfaces with logarithmically growing systole
abstract: We exhibit a sequence of translation surfaces $T_1, T_2,...$ with $T_g$ of genus $g$ and area $g$, such that the systole grows logarithmically with $g$. They are produced by starting with a fixed translation surface, taking covers with the same topology as those discovered by Brooks, and then adding handles by gluing along slits.

title: Asymptotic analysis of sample average approximations for optimal control problems with uncertain dynamics
abstract: We study sample average approximations (SAA) of optimal control problems with control-affine dynamics depending on an uncertain parameter. The objective is an expected terminal cost plus a Tikhonov regularization term, and the controls are square-integrable functions subject to pointwise convex constraints. We show that the reduced objective is twice continuously differentiable in the square-integrable topology, so that no two-norm discrepancy arises, and that its Hessian is a Hilbert--Schmidt perturbation of a multiple of the identity. This yields Lipschitz regularity of stationary controls and second-order conditions without gap for polyhedral constraints. For the SAA scheme with sample size $M$, we prove almost sure uniform consistency of the empirical minimizers, convergence rates of order $M^{-1/2}$ for the optimal values, independent of the dimension of the parameter space. We then derive the asymptotic distributions. The optimal values satisfy a central limit theorem, obtained from a functional central limit theorem for the SAA objective. The empirical minimizers are asymptotically Gaussian when the constraints are inactive; under polyhedral constraints, their limit solves a quadratic problem on the critical cone with a Gaussian linear term. We also derive confidence intervals for linear functionals of the optimal control and illustrate the results on two numerical examples.

title: The Sharp Holder Constant in Mori's Theorem
abstract: Let $K\ge 1$ and let $f$ be a $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ onto itself with $f(0)=0$. We prove that $\lvert f(a)-f(b)\rvert\le 16^{1-\frac{1}{K}}\lvert a-b\rvert^{\frac{1}{K}}$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb{D}$. The constant is sharp, confirming the conjectured value of the Mori constant. The proof reduces the estimate along a Beltrami path to an infinitesimal inequality, which follows from quasiconformal distortion bounds and a three-pole integral estimate.

title: A Proof of the Achlioptas-Friedgut Convergence Conjecture
abstract: For every fixed integer $q\ge3$, we show that the $q$-colourability transition in a sparse random graph takes place at a limiting edge density, thus proving the Achlioptas-Friedgut convergence conjecture. The proof adapts the argument we recently introduced to settle the satisfiability conjecture.

title: Counting formulas and refined generating functions for inversion-sequence Classes 152 and 207
abstract: For the two Class 152 pattern sets, we prove that the common number of inversion sequences of length \(n\geq 1\) is \(a_n=1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\binom{2j}{j}\). The Class 152 proof uses first-descent and last-zero decompositions, with weighted Dyck paths evaluating the resulting generating functions. For Class 207, we prove equality of the three total-count series and give their common generating function as an explicit Lambert-series expression after the substitution \(z=q/(1+q)^2\). Complete legal-site and catalytic recurrences lead to a Lambert series for one class and \(q\)-product orbit sums for another. A cubic limit of the balanced nonterminating \({}_3φ_2\) \(q\)-Saalschutz summation identifies these expressions. Fixed-maximum expansions, finite verification data, refined analytic obstructions, and signed specializations are recorded in the supplementary material.

title: $\mathrm{BMOA}$ and Carleson-homogeneous Denjoy domains
abstract: Let $E$ be a proper closed subset of the extended real line that contains $[-\infty,-1]\cup[1,+\infty]$, and let $F$ be a universal covering of the Denjoy domain $Ω=\overline{\mathbb C}\setminus E$. We prove the conjecture of Huo and Zinsmeister that $E$ is Carleson-homogeneous if $\log F'\in\mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb D)$. The proof is based on an estimate for the length of $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ in terms of the Bloch seminorm of $\log F'$ and a weighted $L^2$ integral of $F''/F'$. From this estimate we deduce that $Ω$ has the Hayman-Wu property, and Carleson-homogeneity then follows from a theorem of Fernández. We also characterize these domains by Carleson measure conditions for the arclength on $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ and for the Schwarzian derivative of $F$, and by the $H^\infty$ interpolation property of the inverse images of suitable sequences in ${\mathbb R}\setminus E$.

title: Polylogarithmic Regret via Certainty Equivalence in Degenerate LQR
abstract: Singular input penalties, as in minimum variance control, can reduce what must be identified to control an unknown linear system. In online linear quadratic control, certainty equivalence can achieve polylogarithmic regret when the optimal controller is identifiable from data collected under optimal feedback. With a positive definite input penalty, however, this condition is restrictive, since for an invertible state matrix it requires all unknown parameters to be identifiable under optimal feedback. We show that singular input penalties relax this requirement, expanding the class of problems in which certainty equivalence achieves polylogarithmic regret. Specifically, we prove that a certainty-equivalence algorithm with a short initial exploration phase achieves $O(\log^2 T)$ expected regret over $T$ interactions whenever controller identifiability holds. We complement this guarantee with an $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ minimax lower bound for a family containing a system where controller identifiability fails. For minimum variance control, knowing the range of the input matrix suffices for controller identifiability, a weaker requirement than knowing the full input matrix, as assumed in prior work with positive definite input penalties. This condition also covers underactuated systems, as we illustrate with a cart-pole example.

title: Beyond the error horizon: averaged quantile Kaczmarz methods for corrupted and noisy linear systems
abstract: Linear systems and least-squares problems can contain measurement errors of different scales: a few measurements may be highly unreliable, while small noise affects every measurement. Residual-based iterative filtering can remove the influence of sparse corruption, but its accuracy is limited by a noise-dependent error horizon. We study how averaging and relaxation reduce this horizon in averaged quantile randomized Kaczmarz (AQRK), which filters equations by residual quantiles and averages a batch of single-row updates. Filtering, however, introduces an update bias that averaging alone cannot remove. We show that re-querying the accepted equations can remove this bias, and when the corruption is sparse enough relative to the conditioning of the matrix and large enough relative to the noise, we prove that AQRK with re-queried residuals reduces the horizon as averaging does without the corruption: its error decays to a horizon proportional to $\sqrt{α/s}$, where $α$ is the stepsize and $s$ the update batch size. Further, decreasing stepsizes or increasing batches gives convergence to the solution of the clean system. Numerical experiments support the theory and examine settings beyond it, including noise that cannot be re-queried and the corrupted low-rank tensor fitting problem. In the latter, AQRK inner solves succeed where standard alternating least-squares solvers and single-row robust updates fail.

title: A refined upper bound on the critical temperature for dilute Bose gases
A Universal $8$-Vertex Origami Torus Triangulation
abstract:
An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat
  torus into $\R^3$. We prove that every flat torus is realized
  as an $8$-vertex origami torus based on the triangulation
  with degree sequence $4,6,6,6,6,6,7,7$. This provides an
  $8$-vertex universal triangulation for origami tori.

title: Permutation groups, derangements and connections
abstract:
What is the chance that a random shuffling of a deck of cards leaves no card in its original place? More precisely, what is the chance that a random permutation has no fixed points? A permutation with no fixed points is known as a derangement. Questions about derangements, like the ones above, go back centuries, but there are also several unsolved problems in this very active area of permutation group theory.
  Based on a minicourse given at "Groups and Algebras in Bicocca for Young Algebraists" in June 2026, this survey provides a general introduction to permutation group theory, with a specific focus on derangements. The survey features modern methods for studying permutation groups, recent developments and open problems concerning derangements and connections between this topic and other areas, such as combinatorics, graph theory, number theory, representation theory and topology.

title: Stochastic differential delay equations with random delay driven by fractional Brownian motion
abstract: We prove an existence and uniqueness result for stochastic differential delay equations driven by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H > \tfrac{1}{2}$, where the delay is a random process. Extending the pathwise Riemann--Stieltjes approach of Ferrante and Rovira \cite{FR2010}, we show that if the random delay $τ(\cdot,ω)$ has almost surely $γ$-Hölder continuous trajectories with $γδ> (1-H)/H$, where $δ\in(0,1]$ is the Hölder exponent of the gradient of the diffusion coefficient, then the equation has a unique solution with paths in $C^{1-α}(-r_0,T;R^d)\subset W_0^{α,\infty}(-r_0,T;R^d)$ for appropriate $α\in(1-H,\tfrac12)$. We also prove that the solution has moments of all orders when $γ>1/(2H)$ and the Hölder constant of the delay is bounded.

title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference II: General convex penalties
abstract:
For smooth penalties and group Lasso, analyzed approximate leave-one-out (ALO) cross-validation by comparing its weights with the trace correction used in mean-field inference. For a $C^2$ penalty $R$, the matrix entering these corrections is $A=[\nabla^2R(\widehat b)+X^TDX]^{-1}$, where $\widehat b$ is the full-data estimator and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of fitted loss curvatures; for group Lasso, the penalty and loss curvatures are first restricted to the active support before taking the pseudoinverse.
  The obstacle to extending this argument to general convex penalties was the lack of an explicit formula for the matrix $A$ entering these corrections. For every finite-valued strongly convex penalty, we construct such a matrix from ordinary derivatives of the penalty response at the observed subgradient. Its projection--pseudoinverse formula separates the response space and penalty curvature, fixed by conditioning, from the explicit design dependence. This supplies the missing ingredient to extend the probabilistic argument of Part~I. The construction recovers the inverse Hessian for smooth penalties and the active-group inverse for group Lasso, including inactive boundary groups.
  In the proportional regime, for Gaussian designs with general positive-definite covariance and covariance-scaled strong convexity, we obtain unconditional bounds comparing both ALO and mean-field predictions with exact leave-one-out predictions in regression and single-index models. The expected average squared prediction error is $O(n^{-1})$, and the expected absolute criterion error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, under bounded, 1-Lipschitz loss scores and suitable test functions. The matrix and ALO weights use only observed data; the mean-field correction additionally uses the design covariance. The construction, recovery identities and statistical guarantees are formalized in Lean~4.

title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $β_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leqβ=β_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $β\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.

title: Avalanche Sharpness and the Stationary State of the Bak--Sneppen Model on $\mathbb Z^d$
abstract:
We establish the stationary picture for the nearest-neighbour Bak--Sneppen model on $\mathbb Z^d$, for every $d\ge1$. There exists a critical level $t_c$ such that, as $N\to\infty$, every fixed family of stationary fitnesses on the torus $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^d$ converges, in exponential coordinates, to independent random variables with law $t_c+\operatorname{Exp}(1)$.
  The proof relies on three estimates for avalanches. For $d\ge2$, these replace the interval structure available in dimension one. We show that the threshold at which the mean avalanche range diverges coincides with the threshold for the appearance of an infinite avalanche, using the hierarchical structure of avalanches and an estimate on the creation of new sites under translation. We then prove that an avalanche reaching a macroscopic distance on the torus can, after any fixed positive increase of the level, be amplified into one covering the whole torus. Finally, below criticality, we obtain exponential integrability of the avalanche range and give a finite--infinite volume comparison.
  These three ingredients allow us to implement the Meester and Znamenski program that connects these avalanche estimates to the stationary law of the finite-volume process.

title: Direct Element-Level Mass Matrix Inversion
abstract: Explicit finite element methods for transient solid dynamics commonly use lumped mass matrices to avoid solving systems of equations for nodal accelerations at each time step. However, diagonal mass matrices may inadequately represent inertia, particularly for higher-order elements and coarse or distorted meshes. This has limited the use of higher-order elements in explicit dynamic analyses. This paper presents a systematic method for directly evaluating the inverse of non-diagonal element-level mass matrices for solid isoparametric elements of arbitrary interpolation order. The method applies to mixed mass matrices defined as linear combinations of lumped and consistent mass matrices, with a weighting parameter controlling the transition between diagonal, consistent, and intermediate formulations. It therefore provides a framework for incorporating non-diagonal mass formulations, including those for quadratic elements, into explicit finite element algorithms. The approach is demonstrated by deriving an explicit inverse formula for the mixed mass matrix of the eight-node hexahedral element. This formula enables efficient element-level inversion without solving a global system. The proposed method can improve inertial representation in transient dynamic analyses while retaining the computational advantages of explicit time integration and is suitable for element-by-element implementations.

title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
abstract: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $ρ$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem
abstract: We place two disks inside the unit disk so that they touch each other and the unit circle. We then insert a disk of the largest possible radius, requiring it to touch both original disks. We show that the smallest possible sum of the three areas is $11π/18$, and find all equality cases. We give three solutions, using Descartes' circle theorem, inversion, and contact-point coordinates. The main difficulty is checking that the third disk is largest among all disks that fit, not only among disks touching the first two.

title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
abstract: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hytönen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(σ)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calderón--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(σ)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{γ_p}$, where $γ_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calderón--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-supremum terms. Together, the lower and upper bounds identify $γ_p$ as the optimal common logarithmic exponent and give the sharp worst-case growth $(1+\log A)^{γ_p}$ under the constraint $[w]_{A_p}\le A$. The results show why information from any one cube cannot fully capture the accumulation of a singular integral across many scales.

title: Positivity in symmetric webs and block permanents
abstract: We use symmetric webs to prove Marcus's block-permanent inequality for up to four blocks of every size, for five blocks of size at least three, and for any fixed number of blocks above an explicit logarithmic bound on the block size. The proof idea is easy: Bending strands in the Schur relation turns the comparison into a calculation with squared norms.

title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width from 1 to 6, reproduces the standard integer and floating-point formats exactly, and comes within 0.07 bits of the ideal at 4 bits. It matches a random-permutation trellis code whose table is thousands of times larger, and exceeds every QTIP codebook. In LLM weight quantization without fine-tuning, CPTC has the lowest KL divergence to the unquantized model at every tested bit width on Llama 3.1 8B and 70B Instruct against QTIP's codebooks (by up to 27%). The decoder has been built into the AWS Trainium 4 AI accelerator, where it runs at the throughput of the native FP4 and FP8 formats for a negligible fraction of the systolic array's area. Fused encoding kernels quantize an 8B model's linear layers in under two minutes on one GPU and, in cycle-level simulation, on one Trainium 4 chip.

title: Hyperkähler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
abstract: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $α$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $σ$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $π:\mathscr M\toΛ$ where $Λ$ encodes $(α,σ)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in an open dense subset $Λ_0\subsetΛ$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(α,σ)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$. For the four-dimensional moduli spaces of types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, we compute these classes to get explicit formulas for the period maps.

title: Remarks on Fourier--Mukai invariances
abstract: This note proves that smoothness and Gorensteinness are Fourier--Mukai invariants for proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. Moreover, a kernel realizing such a partnership is perfect if, and only if, the families are smooth.

title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

title: The injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties
abstract: We prove the injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties over imaginary quadratic fields under some lattice hypotheses. We express integrals of the lift over special cycles as special values of Dirichlet series and deduce injectivity by separating the Fourier coefficients of the cusp forms. We also establish a converse theorem for Borcherds products on $\mathrm{U}(n,1)$.

title: Co-edge-regular graphs with two $λ$-values and four distinct eigenvalues
abstract: A connected $k$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is co-edge-regular if any two distinct non-adjacent vertices have the same number of common neighbors. For adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, let $λ(u,v)=|N(u)\cap N(v)|$. Ge and Koolen asked whether the theorem of Neumaier on strongly regular graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue extends to co-edge-regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues in which $λ(u,v)$ takes exactly two values over the edges $uv$. In this paper, we answer this question. For every integer $t\ge2$ there is $n_t$ such that if $G$ is such a graph with smallest eigenvalue at least $-t$, $n\ge n_t$, and $k<n-2-(t-1)^2/4$, then either $G$ is a clique extension of a strongly regular graph, or $G$ is obtained from a strongly regular graph with a Hoffman coloring by adding all edges inside the color classes. Consequently, $G$ is a clique extension of a strongly regular graph, a $p\times q$ grid with $p\ne q$, or the block graph of a resolvable Steiner $2$-design in which every parallel class is made into a clique.

title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.

title: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture for all exceptional complex reflection groups
abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra. These bases provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

title: Uniqueness of tangent flows in mean curvature flow (I): smooth minimal cone
abstract: We prove uniqueness of multiplicity-one minimal-cone tangent flows in mean curvature flow when the cone has a smooth embedded two-sided link and satisfies strict Hardy stability, radial Gaussian nonresonance, and weighted stationary rigidity. We also establish a discrete Lojasiewicz inequality, polynomial convergence rates, and rigidity among smooth self-shrinkers. In particular, these conclusions hold for all Simons cones $\mathcal C_{p,q}$ with $p,q \geq 1, p+q\geq 6$.

title: Toroidal Obstructions with No K_5 Minor
abstract: Finding the complete set of forbidden minors for the torus remains an open problem. We determine the complete list of toroidal minor obstructions with no $K_5$ minor and prove that there are exactly $74$, each with between $10$ and $14$ vertices. Combined with the known classification of toroidal obstructions with no $K_{3,3}$ minor, this determines every toroidal obstruction that excludes one of the forbidden minors for planarity. The proof uses three-vertex cuts to show that, apart from $K_{3,7}$, every three-connected obstruction in this class has two distinct independent triples, each the common neighborhood of at least two degree-three vertices. The classification proceeds by considering the possible intersections of these triples and reduces each case by planarity tests and enumeration of the possible graph forms. From the $74$ minor obstructions we also obtain a complete list of $381$ topological obstructions for the torus with no $K_5$ minor.

title: Enumerating orbits of finite classical groups on their Lie algebras
abstract: We enumerate the orbits of a finite classical group in the adjoint action on its Lie algebra, giving exact generating functions and very good upper bounds. We treat the general linear, unitary, symplectic and orthogonal groups, in both odd and even characteristic. In even characteristic, we get very nice formulas for the number of orbits on nilpotent classes both in the finite and algebraically closed case. We discuss the connection with commuting varieties.

title: Exotic cluster structures on $Sp_{2n}$
abstract: We modify the seeds of Berenstein, Fomin and Zelevinsky attached to reduced words for~$(w_0,w_0)$, for any simply connected simple complex algebraic group and any aperiodic Belavin--Drinfeld pair. In every type, moves of words act on the resulting seeds by mutations. After a change of coordinates introduced by Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the seeds are, for $SL_N$, seeds of the cluster structures of these authors, and for $Sp_{2n}$ they define regular complete cluster structures with the expected properties. This proves the aperiodic version of their conjecture for $Sp_{2n}$, with its uniqueness part in a refined form.

title: Radial nodal action ground states with two prescribed masses for coupled Schrodinger equations
abstract: We study normalized nodal solutions of a cooperative system of nonlinear Schrödinger equations with two independently prescribed masses. For sufficiently small positive coupling, we obtain a radial nodal action ground state for every mass pair in a fixed compact subset of the positive quadrant. We first minimize the action on a radial nodal Nehari set at fixed frequencies. We then select both frequencies through an interior minimization of the action level. In this way, we adapt the scalar action approach of De Coster--Dovetta--Galant--Serra (\emph{Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire}, 2026) to construct solutions whose components both change sign and whose action is minimal among radial nodal solutions at the selected frequencies.

title: Klarner's sequences have density $0$
abstract: We prove that the set of non-negative integers $n$ which can be obtained from $0$ by repeated application of affine maps $x\mapsto 2x$, $x\mapsto 3x+2$ and $x\mapsto 6x+3$ has density $0$. Moreover, we reach the same conclusion for five other sequences of similar type introduced by D. Klarner. More generally, we establish a criterion excluding stationary measures with bounded density on the profinite group $\mathbb Z_P\cong\prod_{p\mid P}\mathbb Z_p$. A density-to-measure construction using invariant Banach limits and a combinatorial argument involving rational orbits and affine words yield our density-zero results. The criterion also applies to an infinite family of mixed-slope affine semigroups.

title: High-Order Regularization for Singular and Nearly Singular Laplace and Stokes Layer Potentials in Two Dimensions
abstract: Layer potentials represent the solutions of many elliptic boundary value problems, but their kernels have the singularity of the fundamental solution, so standard quadrature loses accuracy at targets on or near the boundary. In two dimensions, Gaussian regularization of the logarithmic kernel gives a smooth kernel involving the exponential integral $E_1$, but for the single layer its regularization error is only first order in the smoothing radius $δ$. We construct modified kernels for two-dimensional Laplace and Stokes single- and double-layer potentials that achieve regularization error $O(δ^p)$, $p=3,5,7$, uniformly for targets on and near the curve. The resulting method is both high-order accurate and easy to implement: the integrals are evaluated directly by the periodic trapezoidal rule on a single fixed set of boundary nodes for all targets. Choosing $δ=c h^q$ with $q<1$, where $h$ is the node spacing, keeps the discretization error smaller than the regularization error as $h\to0$, and numerical experiments confirm the predicted $O(h^{pq})$ convergence. Finally, we combine the near-curve evaluation with a fast Poisson solver to compute the potentials on the entire Cartesian grid.

title: Solution Spaces of the Minimal Surface and Monge-Ampère Equations near Infinity
abstract: In this paper, we study the constructions of all solutions to the minimal surface equation and the Monge-Ampère equation near infinity and the parametrization of these solutions by harmonic functions. It is well-known that Dirichlet boundary value problems in exterior domains do not always admit solutions. We demonstrate that prescribing asymptotic behaviors forms a new type of problem leading to all solutions near infinity. The harmonic functions determining the asymptotic behaviors play the role of ``free data" as the boundary values in the boundary value problems.

title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for $K_5$-minor-free graphs
abstract: Gallai conjectured that the edges of every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. We prove that every connected $K_5$-minor-free graph other than $K_3$ and $K_5-e$ admits such a partition into at most $\floor{n/2}$ paths. The two exceptions require $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. In a smallest counterexample we find a $4$-connected planar part containing four vertices of degree five. Their neighborhoods meet the boundary in at most one vertex. This allows us to apply the planar configurations of Blanché, Bonamy, and Bonichon and to realize the reduced graph as a minor of the original graph.

title: Resistance-regular graphs need not be regular
abstract: A connected graph is resistance-regular if the sum of the effective resistances from a vertex to all other vertices does not depend on the vertex, or equivalently if the Moore-Penrose inverse of its Laplacian has constant diagonal. Walk-regular graphs have this property, and Zhou, Wang and Bu asked in 2016 whether every resistance-regular graph is regular, a question that also arises in the study of graphs with constant resistance curvature. We answer this question in the negative and examine both what resistance-regularity forces and how far from regular such graphs can be. On the spectral side, we prove that a connected graph is walk-regular if and only if the first $m-1$ powers of its Laplacian pseudoinverse have constant diagonal, where $m$ is the number of distinct nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues. Because resistance-regularity constrains only the first power, it forces regularity when $m\le2$ and allows at most two vertex degrees when $m=3$. Any non-regular resistance-regular graph has minimum degree at least $3$ and a connected complement, and an exhaustive computer search shows that it must have at least $13$ vertices. For every even $p\ge4$, we construct a resistance-regular graph on $4p$ vertices with degrees $2p-2$ and $2p-1$, obtaining closed formulas for its Laplacian spectrum and for all pairwise effective resistances. Using module blow-ups, we then construct $n$-vertex resistance-regular graphs whose two degrees differ by $(\sqrt{4n+1}-5)/4$ for infinitely many $n$, as well as examples with three and four distinct degrees, whereas the maximum and minimum degrees of any resistance-regular graph on $n$ vertices differ by less than $n/2$. We close by conjecturing that in a resistance-regular graph the sum of squared resistances at a vertex increases strictly with its degree.

title: Exotic smooth structures on nonorientable 4-manifolds
abstract: We construct closed nonorientable aspherical 4-manifolds with an arbitrarily large number of distinct smooth structures. This uses the reflection trick of Davis-Hayden-Huang-Ruberman-Sunukjian. Our examples become mutually diffeomorphic after either type of stabilization: taking a product with the real line, or taking a connected sum with sufficiently many copies of S^2 x S^2.

title: Banach-Mazur distance and related methods of comparing convex bodies
abstract: The Banach-Mazur distance is one of the standard tools used in the study of mathematical objects such as convex bodies or normed spaces, and it becomes indispensable when investigating properties that are invariant under linear isomorphisms. It appears in convex geometry and convex analysis as a way to quantify the approximation of convex bodies. In functional analysis, it plays a basic role in the study of local properties of Banach spaces. The goal of this survey is to present a cohesive picture of these two perspectives. We supply an extensive collection of known results for reference and list open problems of varying difficulty, which could stimulate further research. We include in our discussion several distinct variations on the concept of the Banach-Mazur distance, some of them exploratory, that haven't received much attention to date in the literature. We follow the trend - which emerged in recent decades - of considering arbitrary convex bodies, and not just those that are centrally symmetric. Finally, we include a comprehensive list of references on the Banach-Mazur distance.

title: A local-local principle for quadratic forms over semiglobal fields
abstract: Given a quadratic form over a semiglobal field, the set of discrete valuations on the field for which the form is anisotropic over the completion is either empty, or it contains a valuation extending that of the base field with a transcendental residue field extension. In dimension at least $3$, this gives a refinement of the local-global principle for isotropy. In dimension $2$, the result yields a description of the set of elements that are locally squares everywhere.

title: Topology of some smooth real Fano threefolds arising from blow-ups along rational curves
abstract: We describe the topological blow-up of a fibre of a Seifert fibration. We then apply this result to determine the diffeomorphism types of the real loci of smooth real Fano threefolds obtained by blowing up either $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{R}}$ or a smooth real quadric threefold along a smooth real rational curve. As an application, we also determine the topology of the real loci of the two real forms of the quintic del Pezzo threefold $V_5$, completing the topological classification of smooth real rational del Pezzo threefolds.

title: When Is Membership Graded? Identifiability and Resolution Limits of a Graded Gaussian Mixture Model
abstract: Mixed-membership models describe each unit as a graded blend of latent types. Before the blend is interpreted, the data should be able to rule out the simpler story in which every unit belongs to a single type. We ask when they can, in a scalar graded Gaussian mixture model, in which each observation is a Beta-weighted convex combination of independent Gaussian draws from two types, the mechanism behind functional mixed-membership models and the normal compositional model. The model is identifiable, unequal variances included, but the identifying information sits in the far tails of the marginal. For the symmetric model we give a closed-form hard-membership mixture that matches the graded marginal in five cumulants, and a Le Cam bound turns it into a certified sample size below which no test separates graded from hard membership with summed error under one half. The threshold is governed by the concentration $c$ relative to $c_0\approx d^2$, where $d$ is the type half-separation in within-type standard deviations. At $d=3$ it is about 2,600 observations at $c=3$ and 77,000 at $c=6$. Most of the difficulty comes from learning $c$. On 100 simulated datasets with graded membership, a correctly specified posterior under the default priors of a published Bayesian sampler for this model class reports hard membership every time, a weak prior gives intervals for the concentration spanning orders of magnitude, and the sampler's own answers depend on where it starts.

title: C*-algebras constructed using acyclic groups
abstract: We show that the free group on countably many generators is not $C^\ast$-superrigid. Furthermore, we realize each of $O_{\infty}$ and the Jiang-Su algebra as a crossed product of a commutative $C^\ast$-algebra. Finally, we construct non-trivial, outer actions on classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras whose crossed products exhaust all classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras. The common theme in the proofs is the use of torsion-free, acyclic groups.

title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high even dimensions
abstract: We prove that the spherically symmetric $SO(d)$ Yang--Mills equation admits a third smooth self-similar profile, in addition to the two known explicit profiles, in every even dimension $d\geq 12$. This complements the analogous existence theorem in odd dimensions $d\geq 11$ (arXiv:2610.36784). In contrast to the odd-dimensional case, where the classification of smooth self-similar profiles reduces to counting roots of an explicit resonance polynomial [Phys. Rev. D 114, 064021 (2026)], the even-dimensional proof requires solving a nonlinear connection problem. In $d=10$, where one explicit profile degenerates to the zero solution, we give a formal argument for the existence of a second nontrivial smooth profile in addition to the single nontrivial explicit one.

title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
abstract: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal Čech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

title: Sharp modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for matrix-valued functions on spheres
abstract:
We prove that for every smooth positive definite matrix-valued function $g$ on the unit sphere $S^d$, \[
  \int_{S^d}\tr(g(\log g-\log\E g))\dd
  \le\dfrac1{2d}\int_{S^d}\tr((Δg)\log g)\dd. \] Here $μ$ is normalized area measure, $\E g$ is the spherical mean, and $Δ$ is the positive spherical Laplacian. This complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality extends Beckner's sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequality, in its modified form, to matrix-valued functions independent of the matrix size. We show that both entropy and Fisher information decay exponentially under the heat flow with optimal exponent $2d$, whose proof combines the Bochner identity with a $4$th-tensor estimate in the matrix-valued setting.

title: Reflection Character Varieties in $\mathrm{SL}_{\pm}(n,\mathbb{R})$ for $2$-Perfect Labeled Truncation Polytopes
abstract: A truncation polytope is a combinatorial polytope represented by a convex polytope obtained from a simplex by a finite sequence of vertex truncations. Marquis studied the deformation spaces of labeled truncation $3$-polytopes, and Choi-Lee-Marquis studied the $2$-perfect case in higher dimensions. In this paper, we consider Coxeter groups associated with non-simplex $2$-perfect labeled truncation $d$-polytopes with connected Coxeter diagrams, where $d\ge3$. For $n\ge d+1$, we study their reflection-generated representations in $\mathrm{SL}_{\pm}(n,\mathbb{R})$ satisfying Vinberg's conditions. Their images in the real GIT quotients of the full representation spaces under conjugation define the reflection character varieties. These varieties and their subspaces of strict characters are semialgebraic, and we determine their common dimension whenever strict characters exist. We also decompose these subspaces by Cartan matrix rank, show that the nonempty pieces are smooth manifolds, and compute their dimensions explicitly.

title: Remarks on thin sets in potential theory for sub-Laplacians
abstract: In contrast to Euclidean cases, we observe that, there are sets in Heisenberg groups that are thin at the origin and block all geodesics from the origin. However, in polarizable Carnot groups, using horizontal radial curves constructed for polar coordinates by Balogh and Tyson, we show that sets, that are thin at the origin, cannot block all horizontal curves. Consequently, we are able to use the asymptotic behavior with respect to the fine topology to estimate the Hausdorff dimension of singularities of potentials for sub-Laplacians and obtain geometric applications.

title: Convergence of discrete exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on surfaces
abstract: We prove that discrete exterior calculus converges for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on every closed oriented Riemannian surface. The proof applies the error bounds of a companion paper on finite element exterior calculus. We prove and use that every closed oriented surface, with any metric, carries uniformly regular families of triangulations that are acute with a uniform margin.

title: Decision-Weighted Limit Theorems: Less Conservative Robust Optimization
abstract: Limit theorems provide a natural way to construct tractable models for optimization under uncertainty. Existing approaches typically apply them to unweighted sums of uncertain parameters and use the resulting bounds to construct uncertainty sets. We show that sharper formulations are obtained by applying limit theorems directly to the uncertain linear expressions in the optimization problem, with the decision variables as weights. For independent random variables with finite variance, the weighted central limit theorem yields a second-order cone constraint with a decision-dependent protection term, and for heavy-tailed random variables governed by stable limit laws, the weighted approach yields power-cone constraints. Using norm duality, we show that, under a condition on the individual bounds, the feasible region of the unweighted formulation is contained in that of the weighted one. In 16,000 knapsack instances with a prescribed violation probability of 5%, the weighted formulation improves the optimal objective value by 20.9% on average, with overall average violation probabilities between 3.45% and 4.95%, whereas those of the unweighted formulation are near zero.

title: An upper bound on non-overlapping codes
abstract: Non-overlapping codes (also known as bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a binary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{5}{6e} +O(n^{-1})\right)\frac{2^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$. This improves, by a factor of $5/6$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Strüngmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).

title: Linearization of nonlocal elasticity based on nonlocal gradients via Γ-convergence
abstract: We provide a rigorous variational derivation of linear nonlocal elasticity from a general nonlinear elastic model based on nonlocal gradients. Under standard assumptions of nonlinear elasticity, we prove that the rescaled nonlinear energies Γ-converge, in the small-strain limit, to the corresponding quadratic linearized energy. The proof relies on a nonlocal geometric rigidity estimate and does not require any global upper growth condition on the stored-energy density.

title: The Conic Tverberg plus minus
abstract: We prove a Tverberg type theorems: Given a set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and an affine subspaces $L_1,...,L_m\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. In some conditions there is a partition $A_1, ..., A_m, B_1, ..., B_m$ of $A$ such that the sets $L_i\cup A_i\cup B_i$ for $i=1,...,m$ have common barycentre with negative masses in $B_i$ and positive masses in $A_i$. The case $B_1=...=B_m=L_1=...=L_m=\varnothing$ is Tverberg's classical theorem. The case $L_1=...=L_m=\varnothing$ gives a partial answer to the question of Barany-Soberon about the possible number of negative masses.

title: Bias-Reduced and Parallel Heavy-Tailed Stochastic Convex Optimization in $\ell_p$ Geometries
abstract: We consider the fundamental problem of parallel stochastic convex optimization (SCO), whose aim is to approximately minimize a convex objective when given the ability to query a moment-bounded stochastic gradient oracle multiple times in parallel per round. Whereas most previous results have focused on the variance-bounded Euclidean ($\ell_2$-norm) setting, meaning the objective is Lipschitz with respect to the $\ell_2$-norm over an $\ell_2$-bounded feasible set in $\mathbb{R}^d$, in this work we study parallel SCO in $\ell_p$ settings for $2 \le p < \infty$ under a heavy-tailed noise model. We begin by introducing a new class of $\ell_p$-optimal-distance-convergence (ODC$_p$) algorithms, drawing on prior stochastic bias-reduced techniques [ACJ+21], which combine with multilevel Monte Carlo methods to efficiently estimate the optimum of uniformly convex objectives. As a consequence of our ODC$_p$ algorithms, we first establish rates for projection-efficient $\ell_p$-Lipschitz optimization, composite convex minimization, and efficient $\ell_p$-proximal point estimation. Combining our ODC$_p$ algorithms with a new $\ell_p$-generalized Gaussian-based stochastic gradient estimator ($p$-GREG), we provide two efficient $\ell_p$ parallel algorithms, EpochDA and $\ell_p$-AC-SA, which achieve optimization error $ε> 0$ with at most $\tilde{O}(d^{\frac{p}{2p + 2}} ε^{-\frac{p}{p + 1}})$ query depth, improving upon the sequential heavy-tailed stochastic query depth of $O(ε^{-p})$ for $ε\leq \tilde{O}(d^{-1/(2p)})$. We also establish dimension-dependent lower bounds of $Ω\bigl(\min\{ε^{-p},d^{p/(3p-2)}\}\bigr)$ adaptive rounds for nonsmooth convex optimization over a subset of the unit $\ell_p$ ball. Our results improve upon the $Ω(\min\{ε^{-p},ε^{2/3}d^{1/3}\})$ bounds of [DG19], when adapted to the same feasible set.

title: Pinned simplex volumes from thin sets in Euclidean spaces
abstract:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a Borel set, with $d\geq2$. We prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H}(E)>d/2$, then there exist distinct points $a,b\in E$ such that the set of triangle areas with fixed base $a,b$ and third vertex varying in $E$ has positive Lebesgue measure. More generally, for $2\leq r\leq d$, if \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}(E)> \max\left\{r-1,\frac{d-r+2}{2}\right\}, \] then there are $r$ affinely independent points in $E$ for which the corresponding base-pinned $r$-simplex volume set has positive Lebesgue measure.
  The geometric input is a thin-plane estimate of Bright, Ortiz, and Zakharov \cite{BrightOrtizZakharov}. For a suitable $(r-2)$-dimensional anchor spanned by $E$, this estimate yields simultaneous Frostman bounds for a projected vertex measure in the normal space of the anchor and for the distribution of directions determining bases that share the anchor. The Peres--Schlag machinery \cite{PeresSchlag}, applied to a local family of distance-to-line maps in this $(d-r+2)$-dimensional normal space, then produces the desired base.
  Finally, we establish an exact correspondence between fixed-base simplex volumes and pinned distances in the normal space of the base, prove a converse for matched bases in layered lifts, and obtain the lower obstruction $\max\{r-1,d/(2r)\}$ for any universal dimension threshold.

title: Hill's Lunar Equation as a Leaf: Riccati Reduction and Frobenius Theory for Second-Order PDEs
abstract:
The equations of Hill and Adams for the lunar perigee and node, Mathieu's equation and Lamé's equation arise as leafwise restrictions of one class of linear partial differential equations, the \emph{square-type foliated equations} $L^2u+A\,Lu+B\,u=0$, where $L$ is an analytic vector field and $A,B$ are analytic functions. Such an equation has a regular singularity exactly when the foliation defined by $L$ is analytically linearizable. At rational saddles, where every point of the indicial conic is resonant, we obtain convergent solutions whose exponents are holomorphic functions of a first integral; their variation describes the monodromy along the leaves and decides when classical Frobenius solutions exist.
  For a Hill equation, the characteristic exponent becomes the value of such a holomorphic function, given by a convergent series. This yields rigorous computer-assisted proofs of Hill's constant for the motion of the lunar perigee and of Adams' constant for the motion of the node: Hill's value is confirmed within his own error estimate and its fifteenth decimal is determined, his value of the motion of the perigee is shown to be correct in all its digits, and Adams' value is confirmed to twelve decimals. For Mathieu's equation, the curves of constant characteristic exponent that govern ion trapping appear as classical Frobenius loci. For Lamé's equation, we prove a product formula for the logarithmic obstructions, which coincide with the leading coefficients of the eigenvalue splittings computed by Volkmer and whose vanishing reflects the finite-gap property.

title: Heat-wave semigroup estimates and the compressible Navier-Stokes Equations
abstract: We study the connection between the heat-wave semigroup and the compressible Navier-Stokes (CNS) equations. On one hand, the parabolic-hyperbolic nature of the CNS motivated the study of space-time estimates for the heat-wave semigroup by using recent harmonic analysis development, in particular, the local smoothing estimates for the wave equations; on the other hand, we apply the new estimates to obtain global well-posedness for CNS in the optimal critical Besov spaces. For the latter purpose, we introduce a new iteration framework for CNS that exploits some intrinsic structures of the equations, so that we can successfully apply these estimates.

title: Real-Rootedness and Log-Concavity of Zigzag Eulerian Polynomials
abstract: We prove that the zigzag Eulerian polynomials have only real, negative, simple zeros, and hence strictly log-concave coefficients, settling the first two parts of a conjecture of Petersen and Zhuang. Real-rootedness in combinatorics is usually proved inside a single algebraic framework, such as interlacing or stability. Our proof rests on a different premise: different parts of a zero set become visible in different representations of the same polynomial, and classical tools suffice once each part is viewed in the right one. The bridge between representations is a local rule. Forgetting the order in which a bounded-jump path visits positions leaves only a nearest-neighbor condition on sorted gaps, which makes an encoding via a transfer matrix much simpler to see. From there the argument passes to complex analysis. The sizes of the matrix's eigenmodes locate the zeros at the two ends of the negative axis, through Rouché's theorem. In a logarithmic coordinate the generating function becomes a combination of derivatives of the hyperbolic secant, akin to the classical derivative polynomials, and the arguments of its nearest poles produce a sine that fixes the signs between consecutive central zeros. The zeros are thus read off from the poles of an associated kernel. More broadly, the proof suggests that combinatorial polynomials defined by local constraints carry analytic structure, in their spectra and in the poles of their kernels, that is complementary to the usual algebraic methods and that classical complex analysis can exploit directly.

title: Differentiable High-Order Mesh $r$-Adaptivity
abstract: High-order mesh r-adaptivity typically entails minimizing a nonlinear functional using its gradients and, for Newton-based methods, its Hessian. These derivatives can be expensive to derive, must be updated with any changes to the functional, and errors in the derivatives directly impact the convergence of r-adaptivity. Additionally, derivatives of the r-adaptivity operator are required for consistent sensitivity analysis for inverse problems. This work develops a framework for differentiable r-adaptivity based on the Target-Matrix Optimization Paradigm. Given a pointwise functional defining the local mesh-adaptation objective, the proposed framework uses $\partial$FEM to automatically generate pointwise first- and second-order derivatives. These local derivatives are then assembled into a global gradient vector and a Hessian operator through the finite element operator decomposition. The derivative kernels support portable CPU and GPU execution, with partial assembly and tensor sum factorization enabling matrix-free application of the Hessian operator. The framework also provides consistent sensitivities of the r-adaptivity operator through automatically generated mixed derivatives and implicit differentiation of the mesh stationarity equations. Numerical experiments show GPU solve times comparable to those of hand-derived TMOP implementations on a benchmark problem, improvement in r-adaptivity convergence due to accurate computation of the derivatives, and demonstrate the use of mesh sensitivities for material-interface identification in an inverse heat-conduction problem.

title: Residual-driven lattice Boltzmann equation. Part I: framework and nonlinear solution methods
abstract:
We developed a residual-driven framework of the lattice Boltzmann equation (LBE) to integrate general nonlinear iterative methods. The nonlinear residual is constructed directly from the complete LBE collision-streaming update, allowing general nonlinear solvers to be integrated without modifying the original LBE algorithmic structure, i.e., the kernel consisting of collision-streaming, boundary conditions, and various forcing and interaction effects. Sophisticated techniques, such as weighted fixed-point iteration, full approximation scheme (FAS) multigrid, and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov methods are integrated into the LBE via this framework, and preconditioned LBE is further incorporated as a nonlinear smoother to demonstrate solver composability.
  Numerical tests validate that FAS and Newton methods do converge to the same discrete steady fixed-point obtained with the primitive LBE iteration. For the 2D lid-driven cavity flow, the FAS scheme reduces the measured solution time by a factor of approximately 44 at Re = 1000 and more than 224 at Re = 5000. Accurate results are also obtained for the steady flows past a cylinder at Re = 20 and the NACA0012 airfoil at Re = 1000. The low Mach-number tests for the flow past a NACA0012 airfoil further show that both the FAS scheme and preconditioning can not only substantially reduce the work required to reach steady solutions, but also mitigate the zero Mach-number crisis.

title: Perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and independence complexes of generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n,2)$
abstract: We show that the perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and the independence complexes of the generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n, 2)$ are homotopy equivalent to wedges of spheres, and we determine the number and dimensions of the spheres. For the former we compute the initial values of Adamaszek's recursion for the independence complexes of cubes of cycles.

title: Structural functional identifiability of unknown differential equation observation maps
abstract: In many differential equation models of real-world systems, the mechanistic structure of the dynamics is known, but the map from the dynamics to the observations is not. This is potentially problematic, as it can prevent us from e.g. learning model parameter values from data. Examples where this occurs include measuring a fluorescent marker as a proxy for the dynamics of a cellular circuit, and using wastewater measurements to follow the development of an epidemic. The nascent field of hybrid modelling, in which machine learning components (like neural networks) are embedded within mechanistic models, provides the tools to learn such maps. Here, the system's dynamics keep their mechanistic form, while a neural network represents the unknown observation map and is trained alongside any unknown core system parameters. This raises a question of identifiability: when can the true observation map be learnt, and when does one simply learn some map that transforms the dynamics into the available data? Building on previous work, we show how structural functional identifiability analysis can establish whether a model's unknown observation maps and core system parameters are identifiable, i.e. can be uniquely learnt from data. We both prove general results on when models with unknown observation maps are, and are not, identifiable, and demonstrate a general methodology (based on differential algebra) for assessing the identifiability of such models. This paves the way for applying classic differential equation workflows to the many real-world systems that contain such unknown maps.

title: Laplacian Eigenvectors of Generically Weighted Graphs Have Pairwise Distinct Coordinates
abstract: Poignard, Pereira and Pade conjectured that, for a generic choice of the nonzero weights of a given graph, the Fiedler vector of the weighted Laplacian has pairwise distinct coordinates. We give a proof that also covers every nonconstant eigenvector. For each connected graph on n vertices we construct a nonzero homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients in the edge weights, of degree n(n-1)(n^2-n+2)/4, which vanishes at a positive weighting exactly when the Laplacian has a repeated eigenvalue, an eigenvector with a zero coordinate, or a nonconstant eigenvector with two equal coordinates. The exceptional weights therefore lie in an algebraic hypersurface, which gives structural genericity in the sense of Poignard, Pereira and Pade; algebraically independent weights are never exceptional, and there are good integer weights not exceeding the degree plus one. The polynomial is a product of Krylov determinants. Its nonvanishing follows by induction on trees: when a leaf is attached with a small weight, a cut identity gives the first-order profile of the new eigenvector and separates the coordinates that coincide in the limit. Exact small cases show that exceptional weightings need not be symmetric.

title: Stokes flow in a wedge with a moving contact point: well-posedness with a fixed contact angle and Navier slip
abstract: We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state. For small contact angles and small initial data satisfying two compatibility conditions, we prove local existence, uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence on the data. The compatibility conditions are the price of the fixed angle for solutions regular in time up to the initial time. Rather than hiding the singularity, the solution class carries it explicitly in corner expansions. The velocity is continuous up to the contact point. The pressure has a logarithmic singularity, the slip-regularised version of that of Huh and Scriven. Its coefficient is proportional to the contact-point velocity. The slope of the free boundary has a corresponding logarithmic correction, the slip-scale counterpart of the Cox-Voinov relation. The linearised problem combines terms of different scaling, which prevents a direct treatment by the Mellin transform. We solve it by a Lax-Milgram argument, and an auxiliary test function problem shows that the variational solution satisfies the equations. Explicit Mellin representations then yield the corner expansions, and the nonlinear problem is solved by a contraction argument.

title: Finite sample guarantees of MPPI: suboptimality, sample complexity and closed-loop guarantees
abstract: This paper considers model predictive path integral (MPPI) control for nonlinear finite-horizon optimal control problems with bounded inputs, allowing nonconvex and nonsmooth costs. We prove theoretical guarantees that quantify the suboptimality caused by positive temperature and finite sampling on MPPI and establish their implications for closed-loop guarantees. Specifically, we derive a suboptimality bound for infinite-sample MPPI that characterizes the effects of temperature and prior coverage, followed by a high-probability finite-sample approximation error bound that reveals the dependence on sample size, temperature, and cost variability. By incorporating these bounds into a terminal-constraint-free MPC framework, we further establish semi-global practical recurrence of the closed-loop system. Numerical examples involving a four-link planar manipulator illustrate the temperature-sampling tradeoff and the influence of prior quality on approximation accuracy and closed-loop performance.

title: Weak error estimates of a spectral Galerkin approximation to the stochastic Burgers equation driven by rough white noise
abstract: In this paper, we investigate weak error estimates for a spectral Galerkin approximation to a stochastic Burgers equation driven by rough space-time white noise. The roughness of the driving noise results that the mild solution possesses only $L^\infty$-regularity rather than any positive-order differentiability order regularity. The theory of classical numerical analysis reveals that the convergence rate of numerical solution is determined by the smoothness of the exact solution, and hence $L^\infty$-regularity is insufficient to yield any positive convergence rate. Indeed, De Vecchi et al.\ \cite{DeVecchi2026} studied a spectral Galerkin approximation to such equation and only proved pathwise convergence. However, we aim to derive positive weak convergence rate for the spectral Galerkin approximation, which is determined by the roughness order of noise. To overcome the difficulty caused by the absence of smoothness of the exact solution, we turn to study the differentiability regularity of the first and second order Fréchet derivatives of the solution to a Kolmogorov equation associated with the spectral Galerkin approximation. We manage to prove that they possess nearly second order smoothness, enabling us to derive a positive weak convergence rate for the spectral Galerkin approximation. Finally, we conduct a numerical experiment to illustrate the theortical analysis.

title: On the Morse index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations
abstract: In this paper, we use the technique developed by the first named author in arXiv:2610.07815 to compute the Morse-index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations. For the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf fibration, we compute the index and nullity, where the metric on the $\mathbb{S}^7$ (resp. $\mathbb{S}^{15}$) is the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf--Berger metric. In particular, for the round metric on the domain, the Morse-index is $45$ (resp. $153$). We also give a spectral formula for the Aloff--Wallach projections. In particular, we obtain that the Konishi $\mathbb{R} P^3$-fibration $N_{1,1}\to\mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable throughout the two-parameter metric family, while the unit tangent sphere bundle $T^1(\mathbb{C} P^2)\to \mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable under some conditions on the metric. We also compute the index and nullity of the Clifford hypersurface in the fiber-squashing range of the quaternionic Berger family. Finally, for the identity map on the quaternionic Hopf--Berger spheres, we determine its Morse--index by an explicit sequence of transition parameters.

title: Gradient estimates and monotonicity formulae for the $p$-filtration equation on Riemannian manifolds
abstract: We derive Li--Yau type estimates on closed Riemannian manifolds and local Hamilton-type gradient estimates on complete manifolds for the $p$-filtration equation $u_t=Δ_pF(u)$. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and a structural condition on $F$, we establish a $\mathcal W$-entropy formula, entropy-power concavity and local entropy rigidity. We also prove a parabolic frequency monotonicity formula without curvature assumptions. The results include homogeneous doubly nonlinear diffusion and extend to nonhomogeneous power sums and the arctangent law.

title: Fixed-Point Results and Disequilibrium for Negators of Hyperbolic-Valued Probability Distributions
abstract: Hyperbolic-valued probability distributions provide a probabilistic setting in which mass, order, and uncertainty take values in the positive cone of the hyperbolic algebra. We study the fixed-point structure of hyperbolic probability negators and the behavior of hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium along their iterates. Starting from a hyperbolic-valued metric on each mass stratum, we define the associated disequilibrium as the separation between a distribution and the uniform distribution determined by its hyperbolic mass. We consider the disequilibria induced by the hyperbolic Euclidean, \(\ell_1\), and Jensen--Shannon metrics. Their hyperbolic Schur-convexity is established and sharp lower and upper bounds are obtained. We also characterize the possible fixed-point sets of hyperbolic negators through an order-theoretic condition and derive criteria ensuring uniqueness of the associated uniform distribution. The behavior of disequilibrium along the iterates of hyperbolic negators is then analyzed through two complementary mechanisms. Domination by Yager's negator yields exact decay factors for the Euclidean and \(\ell_1\) disequilibria and a uniform decay factor for the Jensen--Shannon disequilibrium. Independently, Lipschitz conditions for generated negators lead to positive linear comparison maps whose spectral radii control the asymptotic decay of disequilibrium. These results provide structural and quantitative conditions ensuring that hyperbolic-valued disequilibrium converges to zero under repeated probability negation.

title: Cubic graphs with circumference ratio 21/22 and cyclic connectivity 5
abstract: We construct a cyclically $5$-connected cubic graph of order $22m$ and circumference $21m$ for every $m\geq 3$.
