Consequently, the shortness coefficient of the class of cyclically $5$-connected cubic graphs is at most $21/22$, improving the previously known upper bound of $24/25$. We also demonstrate how I-reductions, which delete an edge and suppress its two end-vertices, can be used to prove cyclic connectivity.

title: FunSearch and Structured SAT Search for Weak Schur Partitions
abstract: The weak Schur problem asks how large an interval of consecutive integers can be partitioned into a fixed number of classes with no class containing a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$ with $a\neq b$. We investigate whether FunSearch, an evolutionary program-search method guided by a large language model, can discover effective construction strategies for this classical combinatorial problem. In our adaptation, FunSearch evolves a priority function used by a fixed greedy solver, while a separate validity check enforces the weakly sum-free condition. This approach matches the known exact values for two, three, and four classes and reaches $WS(5)\geq195$. We then explore a complementary SAT-based approach. Guided by structural information from a 207-element construction communicated by Fred Rowley (Rowley, 2026), our SAT search produces and verifies a distinct valid five-class partition of $\{1,\ldots,207\}$. Thus the strongest construction obtained in this project reaches $WS(5)\geq207$, eleven integers beyond the best published lower bound of 196. The contrast between the two approaches also exposes a limitation of our FunSearch formulation: its greedy solver makes local, irreversible decisions, whereas SAT can enforce global structure across the whole partition.

title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
abstract: A strong edge coloring is an edge coloring where two edges receive different colors if they are incident or joined by a third edge. For a graph $G$, the strong chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $χ'_s(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a strong edge coloring of $G$. In this paper, using a local flag algebra method, we prove that for every graph $G$ of sufficiently large maximum degree $Δ$, $χ'_s(G)\le 1.642Δ^2$, improving the previous best bound $1.73Δ^2$ due to Davey, Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos, Kang, and Volec.

title: New necessary conditions on $h$-vectors of simplicial balls
abstract: Although the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of dimension at most $4$ have been completely characterized, much less is known in dimensions $5$ and higher. We establish new necessary conditions on the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls in these dimensions. Together with the necessary conditions of Billera and Lee and the sufficient conditions of Kolins, our results yield a complete characterization of the $h$-vectors of $5$- and $6$-dimensional simplicial balls. We also give a characterization of $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of any dimension with neighborly boundary.

title: Causal Input--Output Modeling with Prior Information
abstract: We study the problem of inferring a causal input--output model from unpaired marginal observations and a given prior coupling. We formulate this problem using entropic causal optimal transport, which seeks a coupling that preserves the observed marginals, satisfies a one--sided causality constraint, and remains close to the prior. For Gaussian marginals and general quadratic costs, we prove that the optimal coupling is Gaussian and reduce the problem to a finite--dimensional optimization over covariance matrices. Using a Cholesky transformation to simplify the causality constraint, we derive a Lagrangian dual formulation and develop a block coordinate descent algorithm with explicit update formulas. We establish linear convergence of the algorithm, with explicit convergence rates, and prove stability of the optimal coupling under marginal covariance perturbations and derive a statistical error bound. We further show its equivalence to Sinkhorn iterations. Numerical experiments demonstrate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and illustrate the predictive advantages of causal couplings.

title: Multiplicity of Solutions for a Class of Logistic Problems
abstract: The present paper investigates the existence and multiplicity of positive solutions to a class of degenerate logistic problems by combining the Nehari manifold {method} with nonlinear generalized Rayleigh quotients. The quotient associated with the Nehari constraint determines the threshold $λ_*$ at which the fibering structure and the Nehari manifold geometry emerge, while a second quotient identifies the zero-energy threshold $λ^*$ associated with the minimizing solution. Together with the threshold $\barλ$ for the existence of nontrivial solutions, these results yield the strict ordering \( 0<λ_*<\barλ<λ^*<λ_1(Ω)<λ_1(Ω_0), \) showing that the Nehari geometry becomes available before nontrivial solutions {exist} and that the zero-energy transition occurs only afterwards. In the variational range, we obtain a positive minimizing solution on $\mathcal N_λ^+$ and a second positive solution via the Mountain Pass Theorem. Complementary sub-supersolution and truncation arguments extend the multiplicity result to the remaining parameter range. We also establish the sign change of the minimizing energy, the blow-up and normalized asymptotic profile of the minimizing solutions as $λ\uparrowλ_1(Ω_0)$, and the convergence of the mountain-pass level $c_λ^m$ to zero as $λ\uparrowλ_1(Ω)$.

title: Orbital Stability and Instability of Slow and Fast Solitary Waves of gILW
abstract: We study the solitary waves of the generalized Intermediate Long Wave equation (gILW), for a power-type nonlinearity of order $p\geq1$. Using concentration-compactness and symmetric rearrangement, we prove existence of suitable (even, strictly positive and radially decreasing) solitary waves of gILW for every $p\geq1$, and show that, as the depth parameter tends to infinity, they converge in the energy space and in $L^q$, $q\in[2,\infty]$, to the solitary waves of the generalized Benjamin-Ono equation (gBO), while, as the depth parameter tends to zero, after a suitable rescaling, they converge in $L^q$, $q\in[2,\infty]$, to the solitary waves of the generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation (gKdV). Our main results concern the orbital stability of slow and fast solitary waves of gILW, that is, of those for which the product $δc$ of the depth parameter and the velocity is small or large, respectively. For slow waves we obtain stability for $p=1,2,3$ and instability for $p\geq5$ (the same threshold as for gKdV), while for fast waves we obtain stability for $p=1$ and instability for $p\geq3$ (the same threshold as for gBO). In particular, for $p=3$ the stability of the solitary waves changes from one regime to the other. These results extend to $p>1$ the classical result of Albert, Bona and Henry for the Intermediate Long Wave equation ($p=1$). The proof proceeds by perturbation theory, transferring spectral information from gKdV and gBO to gILW through the convergence of the corresponding solitary-wave operators, and in particular avoids any use of an explicit formula for the solitary wave profile, none being available for $p>1$.

title: Michelson and Logarithmic Operator Contrasts Spectral Geometry, Tracial Extensions, and Random Products
abstract: The Michelson contrast of a positive invertible operator is a bounded coordinate for its condition number. Its logarithmic lift, $\operatorname{OLC}(A)=\frac12\log(\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|)$, connects spectral spread with projective Thompson geometry. This preprint collects the Novikov--Nikolaeva series and the associated single-author extensions by Novikov into one treatment. We develop the equality criterion for product subadditivity, its dimension and Jordan-rank thresholds, quantum-state examples, and contrasts associated with unitarily invariant norms. The latter have a sharp additive defect, while the full Schatten family records a logarithmic spectral profile up to homometry. Tracial extensions give characterisations of traces, dimension-sensitive defects, and spectral-edge asymptotics. Unbounded operators are described through critical exponents and finite sections. Tensor, matrix and free independence lead to distinct growth laws for products. Finally, symmetric cones provide a setting for the equality criterion, Lorentz boosts, and Jordan products. Classical ingredients are distinguished from the refinements developed in the series; conjectural asymptotic statements remain explicitly labelled.

title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $θ(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{θ(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

title: Shifted Hankel determinants via Hankel continued fractions
abstract: The Hankel determinants $H_n(F)$ of a power series $F(x)$, as well as the shifted ones $H_n^{(1)}(F)$ and $H_n^{(2)}(F)$, can be read off from its Jacobi continued fraction, provided that all $H_n(F)$ are nonzero. Without any condition on $F$, the Hankel continued fraction ($H$-fraction) still yields all $H_n(F)$. We show that the $H$-fraction of $F$ also determines the shifted Hankel determinants $H_n^{(1)}(F)$, $H_n^{(2)}(F)$ and the backward shifted ones $H_n^{(-1)}(F)$, and we give explicit formulas for them. As applications, we provide simple proofs of Hankel determinant evaluations that were previously established by means of complicated explicit $H$-fractions.

title: Forbidden Substructures Preserved by the Blob Graph Operation
abstract: The blob graph $G^\circ$ of a graph $G$ has a vertex for each non-empty connected vertex subset of $G$, with two distinct subsets adjacent whenever they intersect or are joined by an edge of $G$. This construction has been used in reductions from induced subgraph optimisation problems to maximum-weight independent set, where the preservation of forbidden substructures is essential. We completely characterise the graphs $H$ for which excluding $H$ from $G$ guarantees that $G^\circ$ also excludes $H$, under six containment relations. For subgraphs, minors, and topological minors, preservation holds exactly when $H$ has at most two vertices. For induced subgraphs, it holds exactly when $H$ is a linear forest. For induced topological minors, it holds exactly when $H$ is triangle-free and has maximum degree at most two. For induced minors, it holds exactly when $H$ is triangle-free and every neighbour of a vertex of degree at least three has degree exactly two. These classifications unify and extend preservation results previously established for particular forbidden graphs in algorithmic applications.

title: A polynomial-time decoding algorithm up to half the square-root bound for quadratic residue and generalized quadratic residue codes
abstract: Binary quadratic residue (QR) codes, introduced by Prange in 1958, are cyclic codes of prime length $p\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$ and dimension $(p+1)/2$ whose minimum distance satisfies the square-root bound $d\ge\sqrt p$. They include the Hamming code $[7,4,3]$ and the Golay code $[23,12,7]$, and were generalized by van Lint and MacWilliams to generalized quadratic residue (GQR) codes of prime-power length $q$, for which the bound $d\ge\sqrt q$ still holds and is attained when $q$ is a square. In coding theory, one usually first finds a lower bound on the minimum distance of a family of codes, and then a polynomial-time algorithm decoding up to half of this bound, as for BCH, Reed--Muller or Gabidulin codes. Until now, GQR codes had resisted this approach: no such algorithm was known, apart from individual short lengths. We give a deterministic algorithm which, for every odd prime power $q\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$, corrects every error pattern of weight at most $\lfloor(\sqrt q-1)/2\rfloor$ in the binary GQR code of length $q$, in $O(q^{9/2})$ operations in $\F_q$. We start from a description of QR codes due to Helleseth, which we extend to GQR codes, and in which the syndrome gives the values of the quadratic character of the error-locator polynomial. We then recover this polynomial by adapting to GQR codes the tools that Kopparty developed for recovering polynomials from noisy character values, with the decoding of dual BCH codes as an application. Since the square-root bound is attained when $q$ is a square, this radius is the largest that can be guaranteed uniformly on the class of GQR codes.

title: Obstructions to Hadamard Deformations of Fourier Matrices
abstract:
We study deformations of the Fourier spin model commuting square in the space of commuting squares, or equivalently deformations of the matrix $\sqrt nF_n$, where $F_n$ denotes the Fourier matrix, by complex Hadamard matrices. If $n$ is neither a prime power nor twice a prime, we show that there exist unit vectors in the enveloping tangent space that cannot be realized as directions of convergence of sequential deformations.
  Consequently, the derivative of any differentiable Hadamard family through $\sqrt nF_n$ has rank strictly smaller than the dimension of the enveloping tangent space at $\sqrt nF_n$ (i.e., the defect of $F_n$). This is particularly surprising because for every $n$ there exist enough one-parameter analytic families to provide a basis of directions in the enveloping tangent space.
  We obtain cubic obstructions when $n$ has at least three distinct prime divisors, quartic obstructions when it has exactly two and a repeated factor, and quintic obstructions when it is the product of two distinct odd primes. These results extend our order $30$ result from \cite{HN}.

title: Primal--Dual Kullback--Leibler Mirror-Prox for Dynamic Mean Field Games
abstract: We compute finite-horizon dynamic mean field equilibria using a primal--dual Kullback--Leibler Mirror-Prox algorithm. Each iteration updates occupation measures by exponential tilting and computes the dual correction by solving a linear PDE, without solving a nonlinear Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or a best-response control problem. Under assumptions and Lasry--Lions monotonicity, we prove an $O(K^{-1})$ ergodic Minty bound after $K$ iterations and an $O(K^{-1/2})$ approximate-equilibrium bound for the corrected average. We obtain convergence rates for the population flow under strong monotonicity, and for smooth diffusions with uniformly convex control costs under ordinary monotonicity. We also prove convergence of continuous-time Markov chain approximations to diffusion equilibria and, under additional smoothness and convexity assumptions, bound the error in terms of the spatial mesh size and the number of iterations. Galerkin approximations preserve the $O(K^{-1})$ estimates under suitable bounds on the correction errors. Numerical experiments illustrate the method and its convergence.

title: Forests of Omnitrees: Analysis and Applications to Anisotropic Space--Time Finite Elements
abstract: We prove output-optimal work bounds for omnitree forests, which bisect cells along selected axes. A canonical descriptor characterizes representable partitions independently of split order. Complete one-level cycles, including coarsening, face balance and selected coarse meshes, take sequential work proportional to stored input and output at fixed dimension and key width, with polynomial depth dependence even for unbalanced input. From balanced input, refinement-only balance stays within each request's coordinate slab; this bound is attained. Polynomial trace equations characterize conforming high-order spaces across crossed face partitions. Reconstruction moments bound interpolation errors and capture the logarithmic loss that bilinear nodal interpolation can suffer on balanced meshes. Elements of degree up to four resolve moving heat layers on unstructured 4D space-time and 5D space-time-parameter meshes. Multigrid uses the generated hierarchies.

title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
abstract: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

title: Bounded functions on the character variety for quadratic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
abstract: For any finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, Schneider--Teitelbaum defined and studied the character variety in $p$-adic Fourier theory. It is a rigid analytic curve over $L$ that parameterizes the set of locally $L$-analytic characters of $o_L$. It is conjectured that all bounded functions on the character variety of Schneider--Teitelbaum come from $p$-adic measures. We prove this conjecture for all quadratic extensions $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$.

title: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
abstract: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,β}$ hypersurfaces with $0<β\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

title: On the Kissing Number of Craig's Lattice and Spherical List Decoding
abstract: Craig's lattices $A_{p-1}^k$ are a family of lattices with large kissing numbers, i.e., relative to their dimension $n = p-1$, they contain a large number of shortest nonzero vectors. Specifically, for small $k = o(\log p / \log \log p)$, a lower bound of Bacher (2015) shows that $A_{p-1}^k$ has a super-polynomial kissing number of $ω(n^k)$. Craig's lattices are therefore attractive candidates for the construction of spherical codes. In this work, we introduce a polynomial-time list decoder for spherical codes obtained from Craig's lattices for angular distance below $45^\circ$. Our second main result shows that Bacher's lower bound is asymptotically tight for $k = o(\log p / \log \log p)$. Finally, we introduce an efficient algorithm for computing the kissing number of $A_{p-1}^k$. Using this algorithm, we compute their kissing number in dimensions up to 521. Based on this data, we pose the open question whether the kissing number of $A_{p-1}^k$ with $k \approx \sqrt{p}$ grows like $e^{Θ(\sqrt{n})}$ in dimension $n=p-1$. Concurrent work by Laarhoven and Kominers as well as Bennett, Hhan, Li and Stephens-Davidowitz proves such a bound for very closely related lattices.

title: Normalized solutions for logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equations on graphs
abstract: We study a logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equation with prescribed $L^2$ mass on connected locally finite weighted graphs, with $p > 2$. By minimizing the energy, we obtain a positive solution for every prescribed mass $m > 0$ on finite graphs and, under additional assumptions on the vertex measure and the potential, on infinite graphs. We describe the behavior of positive solutions and their Lagrange multipliers as $m \to 0^+$ or $m \to +\infty$. In particular, as $m \to 0^+$, the minimizers rescaled to unit mass converge along subsequences to functions supported at a single vertex.

title: Global strong solutions to isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations under a scaling-invariant smallness condition in $\mathbb{R}^2$
abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with vacuum at far field in two dimensions. Under an explicit scaling-invariant smallness condition on the initial data, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The scaling-invariant smallness condition implies some classes of large data. The main difficulty is to obtain a uniform upper bound for the density under such the condition. Some new estimates of the dissipation and time-weighted energy estimates with explicit dependence on the initial data are derived, which control the effective viscous flux and close the a priori upper bound for density. In addition, we also obtain algebraic decay of the pressure and the velocity gradient.

title: Synchronized Normalized Solutions for a Critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg System
abstract:
We study positive synchronized normalized solutions to the critical
  Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg system:
  \begin{equation*}
  \left\{
  \begin{aligned}
  -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u)
  &=λ_1|x|^{-2a}u+β_1|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u
  &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(
  μ_1|u|^{p-2}u
  +να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^γ
  \right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,
  -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla v)
  &=λ_2|x|^{-2a}v+β_2|x|^{-bq}|v|^{q-2}v
  &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(
  μ_2|v|^{p-2}v
  +νγ|u|^α|v|^{γ-2}v
  \right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,
  \end{aligned}
  \right.
  \end{equation*}
  subject to the prescribed weighted masses
  \begin{equation*}
  \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx=ρ_1^2,
  \qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}v^2\,dx=ρ_2^2,
  \end{equation*}
  where $N\geq5$, $0\leq a<\frac{N-4}{2}$, $a<b<a+1$,
  $α,γ>1$,
  $α+γ=p=\frac{2N}{N-2(1+a-b)}$, $2<q<p$,
  $β_i,μ_i,ρ_i>0$ for $i=1,2$, and $ν>0$.
  The associated Lagrange multipliers
  $λ_1,λ_2\in\mathbb R$ are unknown.
  Under suitable algebraic compatibility conditions, we establish
  existence and multiplicity results for positive synchronized
  normalized solutions. The construction is based on synchronized
  reduction and critical energy estimates involving a finite-mass
  Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg extremal.
  In the mass-subcritical regime, we find two positive solutions
  with opposite energies when
  $β=β_1ρ_1^{q-2}=β_2ρ_2^{q-2}$
  is sufficiently small. In the mass-critical and mass-supercritical
  regimes, we obtain a synchronized Pohozaev ground state below the
  critical energy threshold for sufficiently small $β$ and for all
  $β>0$, respectively.

title: The Pólya-Szegő inequalities for polygons
abstract: Of the simple polygons of given area with at most $n$ sides, $n\ge5$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity and minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence. The same polygon minimizes the Dirichlet Sobolev quotient for $1\le q\le2$. For convex polygons the proof uses mixed boundary problems on a partition. When there are fewer than $n$ convex vertices, the exterior angles give a lower bound on the torsion deficit. The torsion and eigenvalue inequalities have quadratic stability in Hausdorff distance at fixed area and at fixed perimeter, with optimal exponent.

title: Uniform spatial Schauder estimates for backward stochastic partial differential equations with random coefficients
abstract: We prove spatial Schauder estimates for super-parabolic backward stochastic partial differential equations. All coefficients can be random and depend on time and space, and the estimates are uniform in probability and time. The key ingredient is a weighted conditional energy norm adapted to the parabolic scale of each frequency block. Together with heat-kernel bounds and coefficient freezing, it controls the gradient-martingale coupling without assuming a bounded martingale integrand. As an application, we establish Schauder solvability for semilinear stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations.

title: Nonlocal regularization of sharp-crack energetics: a variational bridge from Griffith geometry to emergent constitutive degradation
abstract: We develop a variational diffuse-crack model based on nonlocal averaging of tensile strain energy. A bounded potential acts on the scaled average, while the compressive energy remains local. The initial slope preserves the averaged tensile strain-energy density to leading order. The first variation yields a constitutive stress in which the tensile contribution is multiplied by the adjoint average of the derivative of the saturation potential. The resulting degradation is therefore determined by the stored-energy functional, without introducing an independent fracture field or prescribing a separate degradation law. For fixed smooth displacement fields with bounded strain, the energy density converges to the classical elastic strain-energy density as the averaging radius tends to zero. The Griffith surface-energy coefficient is recovered for planar opening transitions. A structure-preserving scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) scheme satisfies an exact discrete balance between the modified-energy increment and external work. We compare SAV and velocity-Verlet solutions for dynamic crack branching and Kalthoff--Winkler impact.

title: Doing Well by Doing Good: Alignment of Revenue and Welfare in Robust Product Line Design through Data-Driven Optimization
abstract: Product line design (PLD) selects product variants for a firm to maximize expected revenue. Candidate assortments are usually evaluated under random utility maximization (RUM), in which choice probabilities stem from the joint distribution of latent consumer utilities. As this utility distribution cannot be directly observed and is estimated from choice data, distributional uncertainty inevitably arises. This paper studies how to hedge PLD decisions against such ambiguity. We construct a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model that maximizes worst-case expected revenue over an l1-Wasserstein ball around a nominal utility distribution. We derive a dual reformulation for general nominal distributions and then specialize to two cases. With independent Gumbel utility shocks, the dual simplifies to a closed-form robust multinomial logit. We derive revenue gap bounds for parameters estimated from finite full-assortment choice data. When the true model structure is unknown beforehand, we adopt a data-driven scheme using the empirical distribution of sampled utility vectors and extend optimality-gap analysis to a general RUM oracle. For the NP-hard empirical problem, we propose Adaptive Parametric Search (APS), an algorithm with certified relative optimality guarantees. Numerical experiments show fast computation and better out-of-sample performance.Dual analysis shows that robustness to preference uncertainty endogenously encourages the firm to raise buyer welfare. This incentive takes distinct forms: robustness supports larger assortments in the unconstrained logit setting, whereas under the empirical nominal, it favors products with lower prices and higher utility relative to the outside option. Numerically, we identify a "doing well by doing good" effect: product lines with higher in-sample buyer welfare attain higher out-of-sample revenue and buyer welfare.

title: Hardness and Inapproximability of the Covering Radius for LDPC Codes
abstract: Given a binary parity-check matrix $H$ and an integer $r$, the covering-radius decision problem asks whether every attainable syndrome can be represented by an error vector of Hamming weight at most $r$. We study this problem for sparse parity-check matrices with bounded row and column weights. Using a bounded-occurrence quantified-SAT reduction, we prove that the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-complete for matrices with maximum row and column weight three, and remains $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-hard under a constant multiplicative gap. Starting from Vertex Cover on 3-regular graphs, we also obtain an explicit NP-hard approximation factor under the same weight constraints. We remark that weight three is the exact threshold for hardness: if either the maximum row weight or the maximum column weight is at most two, the covering radius can be computed in polynomial time.

title: Constructions of reversible linear and DNA codes through $T_{D,g}^n-$set and $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$right polycyclic codes
abstract:
In this paper we give a construction technique of $T_{D,g}^n-$set for reversible linear codes and reversible DNA codes with their code parameters. This technique yields many reversible MDS codes which significantly improves the $T^n-$set construction by Oztas et.al. in terms of obtained code parameters. Concatenation-based constructions are presented for reversible linear codes satisfying self-duality and linear complementary dual (LCD) conditions, giving necessary and sufficient condition for desired dual properties.
  We introduce a new notion of $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes. Also, a new construction technique is developed to obtain reversible linear $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes with good parameters (MDS codes) over any finite commutative rings.

title: A Liouville theorem for the Hénon parabolic equation
abstract: We prove that every nonnegative classical entire solution of $u_t-Δu=|x|^αu^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero when $n\ge3$, $α\ge0$, and $1 < p < \frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$. The same conclusion holds for weighted parabolic Gross--Pitaevskii systems with nonlinearities of degree $p=2r+1$ and constant coupling coefficients $β_{ij}=β_{ji}\ge0$ and $β_{ii}>0$. Both results include the unweighted case and require no boundedness, radial symmetry, spatial decay, finite-energy, or growth assumptions. The range is optimal for both problems: bounded nonzero nonnegative stationary solutions exist for $p\ge\frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$.

title: Decision Stability and Model Reduction for Hamilton--Jacobi Navigation in Multiscale Flows
abstract: Autonomous vehicles plan time-optimal routes through flow fields that are known only through reduced, finite-resolution models of an underlying multiscale flow. Classical Hamilton-Jacobi homogenization concerns convergence of the value function as the fine scale vanishes; but what a vehicle commits to is a route, and value accuracy need not imply route accuracy. We study this gap for a fixed-resolution reduction rather than in the homogenization limit. The committed route's dependence on the model-reduction error splits into two regimes. When the optimal route is a unique, nondegenerate minimizer with a regular value-function neighborhood, it depends Lipschitz-continuously on the reduction error, while the extra travel time from acting on the reduced model grows only quadratically with that error. When two routes are tied on the cut locus of the value function, the value remains stable, but an arbitrarily small change in the flow can switch the selected route, making route selection discontinuous in the reduction error. This dichotomy identifies where a reduced model must be accurate: not where the flow error is largest, but where the route choice is fragile. In the regular regime it yields a resolution-allocation principle, while an oracle marginal-regret benchmark illustrates the potential benefit of decision-aware resolution allocation relative to refinement based on flow-error magnitude.

title: On representation-theoretic and homological properties of distance algebras of finite graphs
abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology as bigraded Tor and Ext groups. We study the representation-theoretic and homological properties of the distance algebra $Σ_G$ of a finite connected graph $G$. We characterize the graphs for which $Σ_G$ is representation-finite, multiserial, biserial, or self-injective by an explicit graph-theoretic classification. We also compute the finitistic, self-injective, and dominant dimensions for several natural families of graphs. For a finite modular lattice $L$, we consider the distance algebra $Σ_L$ associated to the Hasse graph of $L$, and show that $Σ_L$ is Auslander--Gorenstein precisely when $L$ is a finite direct product of chains. We also present a family of minimal Auslander--Gorenstein distance algebras, namely, those associated to punctured hypercubes, whose finitistic (equivalently, self-injective; equivalently, dominant) dimension can be arbitrarily large.

title: Stability for a multi-frequency inverse source problem in diffusion-based tomography
abstract: This paper is concerned with the inverse source problem for the time-harmonic diffusion equation arising in optical tomography. In inhomogeneous media, we establish a conditional logarithmic stability estimate by using multi-frequency boundary flux measurements. The proof combines a boundary observability inequality for the associated heat equation with quantitative analytic continuation. For constant coefficients, we further derive an increasing stability estimate with explicit dependence on the frequency bandwidth. In this case, the analysis employs complex polynomial interpolation of the Fourier-Laplace transform of the source. We also implement a multi-frequency Landweber iteration with a discrepancy-based stopping rule to reconstruct the sources. Numerical experiments show an overall improvement in reconstruction accuracy and resolution as the frequency bandwidth increases under the tested noise settings.

title: Maximal defect $2$-blocks with dihedral defect groups up to splendid Morita equivalence
abstract: We classify, up to splendid Morita equivalence, all maximal defect blocks whose defect groups are dihedral \(2\)-groups of order at least \(8\). The classification holds for blocks over an algebraically closed field as well as for those over a suitable discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero. As a consequence, Puig's conjecture holds for this infinite family of blocks. Beyond the classification result itself, a central feature of the present work is the variety of methods required in its proof. Our arguments combine classical techniques of block theory with a broad range of tools and techniques that have emerged over the past twenty-five years. Amongst others these include in a crucial manner the Gorenstein-Walter classification of finite groups with dihedral Sylow \(2\)-subgroups, Linckelmann's glueing of local Morita equivalences to obtain a stable equivalence of Morita type, the modern versions of Fong's 1st and 2nd reduction theorems in terms of splendid and endo-permutation source Morita equivalences, the structure of the Dade group of endo-permutation modules, Boltje-Perepelitsky's extended theory of Brauer pairs for \(p\)-permutation modules, the fusion systems of the blocks involved, or the concrete knowledge of their decomposition matrices.

title: A Brownian web invariance principle: Localized disturbance flows and Hastings-Levitov(0)
abstract: We establish a Brownian web invariance principle for localized disturbance flows, providing a criterion that strengthens the weak-flow convergence of [Norris--Turner 2015, Ann. Probab. 43, 935--970] to path-Hausdorff convergence of their full trajectory collections. We apply this approach to the radial, stationary, and cylindrical versions of the Hastings--Levitov$(0)$ aggregation model, proving path-Hausdorff convergence of the full harmonic measure path collections to the (Cylindrical) Brownian web, together with joint convergence of the full gap--finger collections to geometric embeddings of the corresponding double Brownian webs. This extends the radial HL$(0)$ small-particle limits of [Norris--Turner 2012, Commun. Math. Phys. 316, 809--841] for the harmonic measure flow and finite gap--finger collections. In the radial and cylindrical HL$(0)$, we also show that the rescaled one-arm domination time converges to a multiple of the global coalescence time of coalescing Brownian motion on $\mathbb T$, with convergence of expectations. The main new ingredient is a three-point survival estimate, proved via a multiscale stopping-time decomposition.

title: The Cooperstein conjecture and additive alternating $d$-codes
abstract:
Let $\bigwedge^2 V$ be the second exterior power of a vector space $V$ over a finite field. The Cooperstein conjecture asserts a dimension bound for flats external to varieties consisting of points of bounded rank in $\mathrm{PG}(\bigwedge^2 V)$. This geometric problem can be translated into a question about linear spaces of alternating matrices whose nonzero elements have rank at least a prescribed value. For matrices of odd order, the sharp cardinality bound was already established by Delsarte and Goethals (1975).
  In this paper, we prove the Cooperstein conjecture for matrices of even order and, more generally, we prove its additive analogue by determining, for all admissible parameters, the maximum size of an additive subgroup of alternating matrices in which every nonzero matrix has at least the prescribed rank. Our proof uses Pfaffian equations to characterize alternating matrices of rank below the prescribed minimum. We study the minimal graded free resolutions of the corresponding Pfaffian rings. The Cohen--Macaulay property and the $a$-invariant of each Pfaffian ring determine the largest shift in its resolution. We use trace functions on evaluation quotients to construct polynomial indicators for the matrices of small rank in an additive subgroup. The largest shift controls their degrees, yielding the upper bound by a counting argument. Finally, we give explicit trace constructions attaining the bound.

title: A Divergence-Free Finite Element Discretization of a Convection-Cooling Optimal Control Problem
abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a finite element discretization for a bilinear optimal control problem governed by a stationary convection-diffusion equation, in which an incompressible velocity field acts as the control through the convective term. Continuous piecewise linear finite elements are employed to approximate the state and adjoint variables, while the Stokes-type optimality equation for the velocity control is discretized by a low-order, pointwise divergence-free ($P_1^c\oplus RT_0-P_0$) finite element. To accommodate the nonconforming velocity space, we construct a discrete cost functional by replacing the continuous $H^1$-seminorm regularization with a suitable discrete velocity bilinear form and derive the corresponding discrete first-order optimality system. Since the bilinear coupling between the velocity control and the state variable renders the underlying optimization problem nonconvex, we establish local strong convexity of the discrete reduced cost functional under a second-order sufficient optimality condition at an isolated strict local minimizer of the continuous problem. Furthermore, by exploiting a divergence-preserving interpolation operator, auxiliary state and adjoint error estimates, and a stability relation between the discrete reduced-gradient residual and the control error, we derive a priori error estimates for the state, adjoint state and velocity control. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the optimized incompressible velocity in redistributing the temperature field and to verify the predicted convergence rates.

title: Locking-free numerical methods for poroelasticity optimal control problems with minimal regularities
abstract: We study distributed optimal control of a linear poroelastic system in a total pressure formulation, with displacement and fluid-pressure tracking and box constraints on the source control. A mechanical Schur complement gives well-posedness at zero storage for each fixed finite Lamé parameter, without estimates that grow like the inverse storage coefficient. We discretize the state and adjoint with conforming finite elements and dG(0) time stepping, and use piecewise constant controls. Under the stated regularity assumptions and a positive lower bound on storage, we prove first-order control and state error estimates uniform as the Lamé parameter increases. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates, examine the dependence on the Lamé and storage coefficients, and demonstrate localized pressure control with active bounds.

title: Critical heavy traffic and diffusion limits for shortest-of-d dynamic routing
abstract: We study shortest-of-$d$ routing, with fixed $d\ge2$, in $N$ parallel queues with independent finite-state Markov service environments switching at rate $κ_N$. At the critical load $ρ_N=1-1/N$, the empirical measure of the centered queue lengths, under stationarity, converges in distribution to a random probability measure determined by its mean. We identify the mean's density and the conditional independence of fixed finite collections of centered queues in the limit. On time scales of order $N$, the centered empirical mean converges to a diffusion with explicit drift and constant diffusion coefficient. These limits hold when $κ_N/N\to\infty$, along subsequences with convergent lattice phase. The diffusion limit extends to centered initial empirical measures tight in the first Wasserstein topology, with means converging in law. A short initial layer prepares the limiting family while preserving the limiting mean. Empirical approximation holds in time-integrated Wasserstein distance.

title: Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Constrained Combinatorial Optimization with U(1)-Symmetric Tensor Trains
abstract: Tensor Train (TT) decomposition has emerged as a powerful tool for mitigating the curse of dimensionality in a variety of machine learning and combinatorial optimization tasks. Recent advances show that TT-based generative models can efficiently represent and explore high-dimensional discrete spaces, even when the cost function structure is unknown. However, incorporating hard linear constraints into TT-based optimization remains challenging, as existing interpolation and sampling approaches often fail when feasible points are rare. In this work, we develop a general TT-based framework for constrained combinatorial optimization built upon U(1)-symmetric tensor networks. Our method introduces an expressibility-enhancement mechanism for constructing sparse symmetric tensors and a graph-based diversity measure that guides sample selection during training. On assignment benchmarks, expressibility enhancement and diversity-aware selection improve mean solution quality over their respective baselines. The assignment-selected diversifying strategy also extends to nonpolynomial Set Partitioning, with larger relative gains observed in the higher-tensor-rank data families. Separate runtime benchmarks show substantial speedups over ConstrainTNet and PROTES on non-degenerate assignment workloads; comparisons with simulated annealing depend on constraint information and computational budget, but, overall, support the practicality of the current implementation.

title: Higher orbifold Euler characteristics of torus representations
abstract: We compute the $Γ$-Euler characteristic of a finite-dimensional representation of the compact torus $\mathbb{T}^k$ where $Γ$ is an arbitrary finitely presented group. We additionally compute the $Γ$-Euler characteristic of the unit sphere in such a representation as well as the corresponding symplectic quotient at a nonzero level of the moment map. In each case, the $Γ$-Euler characteristic is expressed in terms of the weight matrix for the representation as well as a description of the abelianization of $Γ$.

title: Helicity conservation for compressible barotropic Euler flows: regularity criteria and a momentum-based approach
abstract: In this paper, we study helicity conservation for weak solutions to the compressible barotropic Euler equations. Using generalized Constantin-E-Titi-type commutator estimates that fully exploit the kinetic energy, we derive new sufficient conditions for helicity conservation across a broader range of regularity exponents. These conditions reveal the interplay between temporal, spatial integrability and differentiability of the velocity and density, as well as the influence of velocity-density coupling on helicity conservation. A key feature of our approach is that helicity conservation is established directly from the momentum equation, without invoking the vorticity equation.

title: $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$
abstract: We give explicit descriptions of the $m$-harmonic polynomials for dihedral groups via hypergeometric functions. Using these, we compute the parameters $m$ for which the Hilbert series of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ differs from the Hilbert series of $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $0$. We also give explicit descriptions of the generators of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ when this is the case.

title: A 5/2 Guarantee for Echelon Stock (s,S) Policies in One-Warehouse Multi-Retailer Systems
abstract: We study a periodic-review warehouse serving multiple heterogeneous retailers with stochastic demand and fixed costs and lead times at both echelons. We construct a deterministic echelon stock $(s,S)$ policy whose long-run expected average cost is at most $5/2$ times the optimum over all nonanticipative policies. The guarantee holds when the common backlog penalty and retailer holding rates are at least the warehouse holding rate and retailer setup costs are at most $3/2$ times the supplier's. The retailer-specific setup-cost condition extends beyond supplier setup-cost dominance: a retailer dispatch may cost up to 50 percent more than a supplier order. Demand vectors are i.i.d. over periods with finite positive means, and demands of different retailers may be correlated. Each retailer selects the full cycle of its single-location plan or a shifted cycle of half its width, and the warehouse serves requests in arrival order, allowing partial shipments. The upper bound on the policy's cost includes each retailer's mirror cost, which prices the warehouse imbalance created by its batching. The upper and lower bounds share a pooled supplier problem and add one problem per retailer, giving a factor independent of all lead times and the number of retailers. For arbitrary nonnegative setup costs and associated retailer demands, a consolidation policy holds allocated stock until a dispatch threshold is met and gives a factor below $4.9$. On 864 instances built from Walmart store sales, the simulated cost of an integer-rounded implementation of the FIFO policy averages 1.45 times the lower bound and reaches 1.75, and our analytical upper bound on its cost is below 1.94 times the lower bound. With no simulation search, the policy comes within 8.2 and 12.2 percent, on average over 216 instances, of an echelon batch policy and an integer-ratio policy, both tuned by simulation for each instance.

title: Noise Characterization and Robust Signal Detection in Yeast Pheromone Molecular Communication
abstract: A critical aspect of Molecular Communications (MC) is the implementation of signal detection policies amidst noise. To date, noise characterizations within the MC field have predominantly drawn from methodologies found in wireless communications literature. In this study, we diverge from existing MC research by utilizing a newly developed experimental platform that employs yeast, allowing us to consider more realistic noise characterizations based on the relevant signaling pathways. We propose suitable signal detection mechanisms tailored to this experimental setup, which focuses on yeast cell-to-cell communications. Our analysis identifies gene transcription as the primary source of noise, and we utilize a Markov birth-death process model with Poisson arrivals and departures to characterize it. The noisy expression of the FUS1 gene is best represented using a mixed Gaussian distribution model. This model serves as a foundation for evaluating the performance of Maximum Likelihood Detection mechanisms in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) for both symbol-by-symbol and sequence transmission schemes. Error analysis indicates that appropriate adjustments to the signal threshold can reduce errors to as low as 10%, which is not negligible. In contrast, the detection of symbol sequences demonstrates enhanced error performance, achieving error rates as low as 0.4%, albeit at the cost of increased computational complexity.

title: A locking-free enriched linearized neural network for linear elasticity
abstract: Neural-network Galerkin methods suffer from volumetric locking in nearly incompressible elasticity. We propose the locking-free enriched linearized neural network (LF-ENN), to the best of our knowledge, the first neural-network Galerkin method proved to be locking-free. Following the enriched Galerkin (EG) method of Yi, Lee and Zikatanov (2022), for finite $λ$ it admits a displacement-only formulation whose trial space is a linearized neural network enriched by one dilation field per element of an auxiliary mesh. The parameter $λ$ enters only through a piecewise constant discrete divergence, whose action on the dilation fields is the graph Laplacian of the dual graph of the mesh. Hence any conforming field can be made discretely divergence-free, and the error is bounded independently of $λ\in(0,\infty]$. The network needs no boundary factor: the Dirichlet condition is imposed weakly by Nitsche's method, and a Galerkin least-squares term on the shear part, as in ENN, together with a Hessian penalty on the elements along the traction boundary, replaces the trace inequality that networks lack. Under the stated approximation and quasi-uniformity assumptions, the discrete stability and error-estimate constants are independent of network width, mesh size, and $λ$, for both clamped and mixed boundary conditions. For solutions with reduced regularity, we establish an error estimate of order $h^s$ under the assumptions $u\in H^{1+s}(Ω)^d$ and $p\in H^s(Ω)$, with $s>1/2$. Numerical experiments, including Cook's membrane, demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in the presence of boundary singularities.

title: Waist inequality and a Hurewicz-type theorem for mean dimension
abstract: We establish a Hurewicz-type inequality relating mean dimension and conditional metric mean dimension. For every equivariant continuous map between dynamical systems, the mean dimension of the domain is bounded above by the sum of the mean dimension of the target and the conditional metric mean dimension of the map. In particular, any equivariant continuous map that decreases mean dimension must have infinite topological conditional entropy. The key ingredient is a new waist inequality, which we believe is of independent geometric interest beyond its application to dynamical systems. Compared with Gromov's original waist inequality, a distinctive feature of this inequality is that it applies to finite simplicial complexes of arbitrary topology, subject only to dimensional restrictions.

title: Growth of Sobolev Norms for Linear Schrodinger Equations with Denjoy--Carleman Potentials
abstract:
We consider the linear Schrödinger equation on a torus of arbitrary dimension with a real time-dependent potential satisfying a mixed space--time Denjoy--Carleman condition. More precisely, for an increasing concave weight \(ω(r)\asymp \log^σ(e+r)\), \(σ> 1\),we assume \[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\partial_t^q\widehat V(k,t)|
  \le Ae^{Bq^{p}}e^{-ρ_{0}ω(|k|)},\qquad
  p=\fracσ{σ-1}. \] The corresponding spatial class is strictly larger than every Gevrey class, while the moment factor gives the quantitative ultradifferentiable control in time needed by the finite normal form. We adapt the method of Delort and Fang--Zhang to this non-power Fourier weight. The essential new point is a quantitative operator calculus whose majorant is built from the moment sequence and an auxiliary factorial that closes the exact Leibniz convolutions. For every $s>0$ we prove \[
  \|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_s
  \exp\{C_s[\log(2+|t|)]^{\frac{1}σ}\}
  \|u(0)\|_{H^s}. \] The estimate is valid for every \(t\in\mathbb R\), holds in every space dimension, requires neither smallness, quasi-periodicity, nor a transversality condition.

title: The Critical Time for Local Controllability of a Water Tank
abstract: We determine the critical time for local controllability near equilibrium of a water tank governed by the one-dimensional Saint-Venant equations and controlled by its horizontal acceleration. With $C^1$ fluid trajectories and continuous controls, local controllability holds exactly for $T>T_c$. In normalized units, $T_c=2+d_c\approx 2.43674$, where $d_c$ is determined by two transcendental equations. In particular, local controllability fails for $2<T\le T_c$, disproving Coron's conjecture that it holds exactly for $T>2$. For times just above $T_c$, we construct a control that cancels the linear and quadratic terms of the endpoint expansion and apply a fixed point argument. At $T_c$, a weighted comparison with a critical plane curve, combined with estimates along the nonlinear characteristics, gives the obstruction.

title: Approximation numbers of Hankel Operators on Weighted Fock Spaces and the Berger--Coburn Phenomenon
abstract:
Let $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb{C}^n)$ be a real-valued weight whose real Hessian is uniformly positive definite and bounded. For $0<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and possibly unbounded symbols $f$, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for prescribed decay of the approximation numbers of Hankel operators $H_f$ from weighted Fock spaces $F^p(\varphi)$ to weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^q(\varphi)$ in terms of the non-increasing rearrangement of the IDA function of $f$. We also characterize membership in the approximation ideals $\mathfrak A_s(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ and their weak counterparts $\mathfrak A_{s,\infty}(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ for $0<s<\infty$. The symbol criteria involve Lorentz, Lorentz--Zygmund, and Copson--Lorentz spaces. Our approach also yields the converse to the sufficient condition in [15], thereby completing the characterization of prescribed singular value decay for Hankel operators on a broad class of weighted Bergman spaces.
  For the pair $H_f$ and $H_{\bar f}$ on weighted Fock spaces, we characterize simultaneous decay of their approximation numbers and simultaneous membership in these ideals in terms of the mean oscillation function of $f$. For bounded symbols, we establish the Berger--Coburn phenomenon for both ideals in sharp exponent ranges. A new feature in the case $p<2<q$ is that the Berger--Coburn equivalence holds for $s_0(p,q)<s\le1$, where the sharp threshold $s_0(p,q)$ is strictly less than $1$.

title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
abstract:
A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved. However, very few results are known for graphs with maximum degree four or more. Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana showed that every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{19})$-packing edge-coloring and a $(1^2,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring.
  In this paper, we improve the results of Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana by showing every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. As a corollary of our result, every graph with degree at most four has a $(1^2,2^{16})$-packing edge-coloring.

title: OCP: a greedy projection method for row-sparse representations of minimum-norm solutions
abstract: In this paper, we propose a greedy projection method, termed orthogonal constraint pursuit (OCP), for identifying a small set of rows of a consistent linear system $Ax=b$ whose span contains the minimum-norm solution $x^*$, along with the coefficients of that representation. The method successively activates the most violated constraint, and then projects the iterate onto the intersection of all activated constraints. We prove that OCP is equivalent to OMP applied to the dictionary $A^T$ and the signal $x^*$, and that it terminates in at most rank(A) iterations. When $x^*$ is a linear combination of $s$ rows of a matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed on the unit sphere, OCP identifies those rows in exactly $s$ iterations with probability $1-O(m^{-1})$, provided that $n\ge Cs\ln m$ for a sufficiently large constant $C$. We also derive a variant of OCP with constraint removal for hard-margin support vector machines with regularized bias, which returns the support vectors, along with the multipliers that satisfy the KKT conditions. Numerical results on both real and synthetic problems demonstrate the identification of representing rows and the regime in which it is competitive with Krylov subspace methods.

title: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
abstract: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line. The 19 displayed algebraic certificates comprise 18 improvements and one closed-form reproduction; they include HJ(4,3)>=164, HJ(5,4)>=7418, and HJ(5,6)>=34034. The underlying period-p construction also proves kappa_ow(t,r)>=p-1 for the one-weight bracket ceiling, in particular kappa_ow(5,4)>=7416 and kappa_ow(5,6)>=34032. Warm breakout-weighted tabu search on the type simplex gives HJ(3,4)>=51. Whole-colouring local search gives W(8,3)>522, W(11,3)>1193, and W(17,3)>3620. All accepted certificates are available separately and are checked by direct enumeration; unresolved searches are reported as UNKNOWN, not UNSAT.

title: Cyclic group actions on K3 surfaces and almost complex structures
abstract: Fintushel, Stern and Sunukjian constructed exotic $\mathbb{Z}_n$-actions on $K3$ for $n=2,3,4$ using twist-rim surgery. We prove that these exotic actions do not preserve any Ricci flat metric or any integrable complex structure. This answers a question of Farb and Looijenga in the negative. In contrast, we prove that any smooth $\mathbb{Z}_n$-action on $K3$ for which the fixed point set has only non-isolated fixed points preserves an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class. In particular, this applies to the Fintushel-Stern-Sunukjian examples. Lastly, we classify the possible fixed point data and action on cohomology for cyclic group actions on $K3$ of prime order which preserve an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class.

title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
abstract: We prove the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume bound for lattice polytopes with $k\ge3$ interior lattice points: the Euclidean volume of such a lattice polytope is at most $6(k+1)$, with equality if and only if the polytope is affinely unimodularly equivalent to $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,3e_2,6(k+1)e_3)$. The inequality is strict when the minimum lattice width is at least three. Together with the known cases $k=1,2$, this completely resolves the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture.

title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
abstract: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calderón--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

title: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
abstract: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$. Fixing the order of all differences splits the real problem into finitely many polyhedral chambers. A branch-and-bound over these chambers, with an exact rational certificate at every leaf, proves $G_R(n) = G_Z(n)$ for $n \le 10$. Each proof takes under a minute and is verified by an independent checker that uses only exact arithmetic. An exhaustive exact enumeration of all chamber vertices confirms the result for $n \le 7$, and shows that there the shortest real rulers are exactly the optimal integer rulers and their mirror images. For every $n$ we show $n(\sqrt{n}-1)^2 \le G_R(n) \le G_Z(n)$, so that $G_R(n) \sim G_Z(n) \sim n^2$. Non-integral chamber vertices first appear at $n = 7$: there are 84, all half-integral. Already there, 80 of them are shortest points of their chambers, 40 of them the only one, although the global optimum is integral; a twelve-mark example of the same kind comes from Singer's construction. On the other hand, every Singer ruler with at most 104 marks, cut at the largest gap, is the only shortest point of its own chamber; we conjecture this for all prime powers.

title: Maximin Dispersion over Simple Polyhedral Domains: Strong NP-Completeness and Exact Algorithms
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the decision version of weighted maximin dispersion over the unit $\ell_1$-ball with rational sites and positive rational weights is strongly NP-complete. The same holds for unweighted dispersion over full-dimensional integer simplices when the sites are exactly their vertices. Both reductions from Exact Cover by 3-Sets rely on a shared quadratic rigidity argument. We also give exact algorithms that run in polynomial time for every fixed dimension. For the simplex problem, a Voronoi decomposition yields rational optimal solutions. For the weighted $\ell_1$-ball problem, an orthant decomposition and a single-paraboloid lifting yield optimal solutions whose coordinates lie in a common real algebraic extension of degree at most two. In both cases, these solutions have polynomial encoding length and provide certificates for NP membership.

title: Global existence and semi-classical limit for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation
abstract: In this paper, we study the global existence and the semi-classical limit of the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation. We first establish the existence and uniqueness of a global weak solution for initial data with finite mass and second velocity moment satisfying the Pauli bound. When the initial datum also has finite spatial second moment and finite free energy, we prove that the solution satisfies the Fermi--Dirac free energy inequality. Next, as the quantum parameter $\hbar$ goes to zero, we prove that the solution of the Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation converges strongly to the classical Fokker--Planck solution in $\mathcal C([0,T];L^1_j(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d))$ for all $j\in[0,2)$. We also obtain a quantitative convergence rate in $\hbar$ when both equations share the same bounded initial datum.

title: Asymptotic enumeration of histories and limit laws in two random graph evolution models
abstract:
We study growth models for random graphs where the growth is established by vertex or edge creations and where there is no dependence between vertices and edges. Creations are logged by time stamps such that the history of the resulting graph can be reconstructed. We investigate two prototypical models, an undirected and a directed one, called undirected independent growth model (UIG-model) and directed independent growth model (DIG-model). The generating functions for the number of histories have radius of convergence equal to zero. In the UIG-model, we express the asymptotic number of histories as a sum that is amenable to the discrete Laplace method. We derive the asymptotic number of histories, study the number of vertices of a random history, and prove a central limit theorem.
  In the DIG-model we use a rescaled Borel transform to get an entire function. Then we show that this function is Hayman admissible, which enables us to derive the asymptotic number of histories in this model. The counting sequence is closely related to the framework of generalized Legendre-Stirling numbers. To determine the number of vertices in a random history, we prove that the bivariate generating function is e-admissible and infer that again a normal limit law holds. Finally, we discuss a correspondence to set partitions with even block sizes and present an algorithm based on Boltzmann samplers that generates such graphs uniformly at random.

title: Equivariant Flow Matching on Homogeneous Spaces
abstract: Flow matching enables the training of networks that can flow samples from an initial to a target distribution. The network is regressed against simple vector fields that are conditioned on end points in the target distribution. In the Euclidean case, these conditional vector fields induce flows along straight lines. Various generalisations have been proposed to perform flow matching on spaces where straight lines are not well-defined, such as Riemannian manifolds and Lie groups. Riemannian flow matching applies to many domains, but typically requires expensive simulation, while flow matching on Lie groups is simulation-free but only works on Lie groups. In this work, we develop equivariant flow matching on homogeneous spaces, which generalises flow matching on Lie groups, while remaining simulation-free. We also derive all generators connecting pairs of position-orientations, generalising, and perform a similar derivation for event-velocity space, the Lorentzian analogue of position-orientation space, so that we can perform flow matching on these spaces.

title: On the volume growth assumption in the Eulerian definition of RCD spaces
abstract: We prove that every infinitesimally Hilbertian metric measure space whose reference measure is a Radon measure, and which satisfies the Sobolev-to-Lipschitz property and the weak Bochner inequality with a lower Ricci bound, has Gaussian volume growth; in particular, balls have finite measure. Hence, in the Eulerian definition of $\mathsf{RCD}(K,\infty)$ spaces, both the volume growth assumption and the finiteness of the measure of balls are redundant. The proof combines the self-improvement of the Bakry--Émery gradient estimate, obtained without using the conservation of mass of the heat flow, with a dimension-free Harnack inequality derived from the Sobolev-to-Lipschitz property.

title: A new premodel for bounded type Siegel disks of some transcendental entire functions
abstract:
In the 1980s, Douady and Sullivan conjectured that the Siegel disks of rational maps with degree at least two are Jordan domains. Based on the study of Blaschke models, this conjecture was settled by Zhang under the condition that the Siegel disks are of bounded type, and by Zakeri for a large number of transcendental entire functions under the same condition. The entire functions studied by Zakeri have exactly one finite asymptotic value, which is the center of the fixed Siegel disk. Chéritat, and later with Epstein, also studied the Siegel disk boundaries of such type transcendental entire functions by developing Ghys-like models.
  In this paper, by introducing a new premodel, we prove that the fixed bounded type Siegel disk centered at the non-zero point $λ-1$ of $f_λ(z)=e^{1-λ}ze^z$ is a quasi-disk whose boundary contains the critical point $-1$. The asymptotic value $0$ is not contained in the Siegel disk of these entire functions, which is essentially different from the previous results. Moreover, we prove that the Julia sets of these functions with a fixed bounded type Siegel disk are locally connected.

title: Subsystem Stabilizer $(r,δ)$-Locally Recoverable Codes: Characterization, Bounds and Constructions
abstract: Local erasure recovery limits the number of physical systems accessed to repair a distributed quantum memory. For subsystem stabilizer codes (SSCs), a basic question is whether erasures can be corrected within a prescribed repair set. In this paper, we study subsystem stabilizer $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes ($(r,δ)$-SSLRCs), in which each coordinate belongs to a repair set of size between $δ$ and $r+δ-1$ that corrects any set of up to $δ-1$ erasures while preserving the logical subsystem and allowing the gauge subsystem to change. We first characterize local erasure recovery algebraically and apply this criterion to Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) and Hermitian hull constructions for $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs. For $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs, without assuming purity, we derive a redundancy bound for disjoint repair sets, a supported-subspace bound based on supported stabilizer and gauge subspaces, and a mixed counting bound for known erasures within selected repair sets and errors at unknown positions outside their union. For pure $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs with overlapping repair sets, we establish the Singleton-type and alphabet-dependent bounds, together with explicit Griesmer, Hamming, and Plotkin bounds. Moreover, we construct nine classes of $\F_q$-linear pure $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs from maximum distance separable (MDS) stabilizer codes, Reed-Solomon (RS) codes, and linear codes with MDS Hermitian hulls, which are simultaneously optimal with respect to several bounds for $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs.

title: An Explicit Parallelizable Robin-Robin Splitting Scheme for Navier-Stokes-Naghdi Shell Interaction
abstract: We develop a novel explicit Robin-Robin splitting scheme for the system of an incompressible viscous fluid coupled to a time dependent Naghdi shell model. The shell model includes three displacement components and three independent rotation components, accounting for membrane, bending, and transverse-shear deformations. Both Robin conditions depend only on interface data from the previous time step, allowing the fluid and shell subproblems to be solved independently without coupling subiterations. For the fixed-domain Stokes-Naghdi problem, we derive a discrete energy identity that incorporates shell rotational inertia, interface velocities, and interface loads. We prove that the scheme is unconditionally stable for any fixed positive common Robin coefficient under homogeneous external data. Under suitable regularity and initialization assumptions, we establish first-order consistency and an $O(\sqrt{Δt})$ temporal error bound in the mechanical energy norm. Numerical experiments with a moving-domain pressure pulse compare the proposed scheme with the kinematically coupled $β$-scheme and a monolithic solver. To demonstrate its applicability to a more realistic vascular configuration, we simulate a stented artery using a bonded layered shell with stiff strut bands, capturing spatial variations in the arterial wall response.

title: On continuous unitriangular matrices on \(\mathbb R^2\)
abstract: Let \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) be the group of complex \(2\times 2\)-matrices with determinant \(1\). We prove that each continuous map \(A:\R^2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\C)\) can be written in the form \[A=\begin{pmatrix}1&f_1\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_2&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_3\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\f_4&1\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&f_5\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \] where \(f_1,\ldots,f_5:\R^2\to\C\) are continuous functions.

title: Towards the componentwise three-soliton conjecture: cones, collisions, soft momenta and graphs
abstract: The componentwise three-soliton conjecture of Part~I states that if an even polynomial $P$ with $P(0)=0$ satisfies Hirota's three-soliton condition on a non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one of its dispersion variety, then it satisfies the $N$-soliton condition there for every $N$. We prove restrictions on components carrying this condition and classify the polynomials satisfying it on several families of components, with no degree bound. Restrictions: if the top homogeneous part of the equation of the component has a nonlinear irreducible factor, then $P$ is a multiple of a quadratic form; the order of $P$ at the origin is tied to the multiplicities of the component and of the doubled component; a component through the origin has odd multiplicity; the condition passes to all limits of the rescaled component, and the Newton polygon of a plane component has edges of only ten directions. Classifications: on the cubic graph $v=u^3$, where the four-soliton condition holds exactly in multiplicity one; on the graphs $v=q(u)$ with $°q\ge3$, where $P$ exists only if $q$ is an odd cubic or an odd quintic, so the conjecture holds for all graphs of polynomials; and for three families of Hietarinta's list, where each irreducible member is, up to a constant factor, the only such polynomial on its dispersion variety. All three satisfy the $N$-soliton condition for every $N$, so the conjecture holds for them: two belong to the BKP hierarchy, and for Hietarinta's quartic equation, known to satisfy it for $N\le4$, we prove it by fusing resonant momenta and counting zeros on its curve. For translated hyperbolas we exclude the one through the origin and all $P$ of degree at most eight. The solutions of multiplicity one on graphs are known bilinear equations; new is that there are no others. The conjecture remains open.

title: Extremal metrics for the $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalues
abstract: We study the $G$-invariant Steklov spectrum of compact connected Riemannian manifolds with boundary, endowed with an effective isometric action of a compact Lie group $G$. Under a mild nontransitivity assumption on the boundary action, we establish that this spectrum consists of an infinite sequence of eigenvalues diverging to infinity. We then investigate extremal metrics for the normalised $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue functionals. Assuming that $\dim G \geq 1$, we prove that none of these functionals admits an extremal $G$-invariant metric. Moreover, when $\dim M \geq 3$, the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue is unbounded above even within a fixed $G$-invariant conformal class. The proof relies on a local model near a boundary orbit and spectral convergence under conformal collapse. Finally, in contrast with the upper bounds obtained by Colbois, Dryden and El Soufi for invariant Laplace eigenvalues of embedded spheres of revolution, we construct, for any $n \geq 3$, a sequence of smooth Euclidean domains of revolution in $\mathbb R^n$, all diffeomorphic to the ball, along which the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue blows up.

title: B-Series Theory for Continuous Time Integration Methods
abstract: B-Series are a common tool for constructing numerical integration methods and partitioned variations. In this paper, we expand the operations of B-Series to describe the formal expansion of modified differential equations found in multirate ODE solvers. Typically, such modified differential equations have time dependent approximations using summed fixed constant states. To create the B-Series we introduce a new operation called replacement to induce the constant states and add a time parameterization to the labels of the B-Series. By doing so we introduce new analysis via the permanent and block matrices which provide alternative formulations to composition and substitution. To support the time dependent labels properties are provided, the exact solution is described in Tree Iterated Integrals, and the underlying approximate representations are analyzed.

title: The topology of the mean action spectrum
abstract: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.

title: Solution-Set Properties of Absolute Value Equations: Inverse Nonnegativity, Boundedness, and Connectedness
abstract:
The solution-set properties of the absolute value equation (AVE) \(Ax+|x|=b\) were systematically investigated by Hladík (\emph{SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl.} \textbf{44}, 175-195, 2023), who also formulated several related open questions. This paper settles and extends some of those questions. A complete converse characterization of inverse nonnegativity is established without restrictions on the matrix order
  or symmetry. The characterization is accompanied by equivalent
  criteria involving nonsingular \(M\)-matrices and spectral radii.
  A diagonal semidefinite certificate is then developed for the uniform
  boundedness of solution sets. Unlike regularity conditions, this
  certificate permits infinitely many solutions, as illustrated by a
  three-dimensional example whose solution set contains a nontrivial
  line segment. Connectedness of the solution set for an individual
  right-hand side is characterized through a finite graph formed from
  its orthant components. A further sufficient condition is obtained
  from the \(P_0\)-property of the associated complementarity matrix.
  The inverse-nonnegativity characterization is finally extended to
  generalized absolute value equations (GAVE) having a nonnegative
  absolute-value coefficient matrix.

title: Abelian varieties with homotheties
abstract: In 1980, Bogomolov proved that the $\ell$-adic Galois image of an Abelian variety over a number field contains an open subgroup of the homotheties. In 1986, Serre refined that result, showing that the homotheties coming from the Galois side were uniformly bounded in $\ell$ inside the homotheties of the codomain of the representation. In a 2007 paper, Zarhin shows that Bogomolov's conclusion can fail in non-trivial cases for global function fields. We prove a suitable analogue of Serre's results over finitely generated fields of positive characteristic. As a consequence, we prove a new case of the 1978 conjecture by Geyer and Jarden.

title: Global phase-plane organization of a toxin-mediated plant-herbivore model
abstract: Plant-herbivore interactions with chemical plant defence mechanisms can generate complex population dynamics through the nonlinear interplay between resource availability, herbivore pressure, and defence-induced feedbacks.
